# Smartchat Docs

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/

> Documentation for T-Systems Smartchat.

The T-Systems Smartchat is an AI chatbot application. Smartchat enables secure interaction with your own data sources using natural language. You can search documents for information, summarize their content, and generate new content or specific output formats based on them.

The technical foundation is a **Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)** architecture. RAG retrieves information from files or databases and provides it to the language model (Large Language Model, LLM) as context. This means chat responses are grounded in the retrieved content. Smartchat displays the name of each source used.

> **Data privacy**
>
> The language models used in Smartchat are **not** trained on user inputs. Data processing takes place in a secure cloud environment within the EU, operated by Telekom and hosted in T-Cloud Public. A [selection of LLMs](https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/plans/) is available and continuously updated with the latest models.
>
> Data you mark as [confidential](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/) is processed only by Telekom-hosted models and is never sent to external providers.

[FAQ ](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/)Answers to common questions about integrations, security, Spaces, large document collections and models.

[User Documentation ](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/)Getting started, knowledge collections, assistants, Deep Dive, agents and administration.

Multi-Tenancy

Fully isolated tenants (Spaces) with separate users, documents, and configurations — all on a single deployment.

Confidential Data

Mark a collection or a whole Space as confidential and Smartchat keeps it on Telekom-hosted models: no externally hosted models, no web search, no sharing.

Enterprise RBAC

Fine-grained role-based access control across spaces, admin panels, and API endpoints — synced with your SSO provider.

Async Ingestion Pipeline

Scalable, fully asynchronous document ingestion — handles large document volumes without blocking.

Security Hardening

Sandboxed code execution, input validation, and attack surface reduction beyond upstream defaults.

Compliance & Accessibility

Certified for enterprise compliance standards and accessibility requirements.

Confluence Integration

Connect Confluence Data Center spaces — pages are auto-synced and become searchable context in chats.

---

# FAQ

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/

> Answers to common questions about Smartchat — integrations, security, Spaces and groups, large document collections, skills and models.

Short answers to common questions about Smartchat.

## [Account and sign-in](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#account-and-sign-in)

### [My login link has expired. What should I do?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#my-login-link-has-expired-what-should-i-do)

Use **Forgot Password** on the Smartchat login screen. Enter your e-mail address, and you receive an e-mail with a new link to set your password. See also [Registration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/getting-started/#registration).

## [Integrations and solution development](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#integrations-and-solution-development)

### [Can Smartchat connect to tools installed on a user’s computer?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#can-smartchat-connect-to-tools-installed-on-a-users-computer)

Not directly. Smartchat runs in the cloud and cannot reach software installed on a single laptop.

Tools and data sources are connected through the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/), as [connectors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/) for agents:

- We do not run or provide MCP servers. Smartchat connects existing MCP servers that your organization manages and that are reachable over the internet.
- MCP servers must support Dynamic Client Registration.
- An administrator makes each connector available. Users then authorise their own access to it.

If your organization runs an MCP server for a tool and that server is reachable over the internet, an agent can work with the tool.

Agent Mode and connectors are currently in preview.

### [Can users build their own projects, connect them to GitHub and host applications such as HTML pages?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#can-users-build-their-own-projects-connect-them-to-github-and-host-applications-such-as-html-pages)

An agent works in an isolated sandbox, a separate virtual machine per user, with a file system and a terminal. It can write and run code, create and convert files, run data analyses and use the web. Files it produces come back into the chat.

- The sandbox is a workspace for the length of a task, not a permanent development environment.
- Smartchat is not a hosting platform. Results such as an HTML page can be downloaded and deployed on your own servers.
- Alternatively, you can connect an MCP server that lets the agent upload reports or other results to your own systems for publishing. GitHub is connected the same way, through an MCP server.

### [How does Smartchat compare with Codex or other coding agents?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-does-smartchat-compare-with-codex-or-other-coding-agents)

Codex and similar coding agents are built for software development: they work directly in a repository and in the developer’s tools. Smartchat’s agent is general-purpose. Its strengths are working with your documents and knowledge collections, analysis and producing files, with the data staying in a controlled environment.

For ongoing software development, a dedicated coding tool is the better choice, and Smartchat complements it. T-Systems offers [AI Engineer](https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/aie/overview/) for that, a set of AI tools for software developers, including IDE integrations, command-line tools and MCP integrations.

## [Security and data protection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#security-and-data-protection)

### [How is data protected and processed?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-is-data-protected-and-processed)

- Smartchat is hosted by T-Systems on T-Cloud Public in Germany. Each customer has its own environment.
- Data sent to models hosted by T-Systems, and the results they return, are not stored, are not visible to T-Systems or third parties, and are not used for training.
- Requests to models from external providers go to that provider and are processed on its infrastructure. The provider’s own data processing terms apply.
- Data can be marked [confidential](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/), for a single collection or for the whole Space. For confidential data, all external models and web search are switched off, so only models hosted by T-Systems can be used.
- [Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/) keep data separated, and access is controlled by [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/). Sign-in is through local accounts or your organization’s SSO (OIDC). All connections use HTTPS.

Hosting is in the EU, so it is covered by the GDPR and by Telekom’s Privacy and Security Assessment (PSA). The PSA governs GDPR, data privacy, security and accessibility compliance. If your organization is outside the EU, check this against your own rules for cross-border processing.

### [Does Smartchat support two-factor authentication?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#does-smartchat-support-two-factor-authentication)

Yes. Two-factor authentication is enabled by default for every account that can perform privileged actions, such as administrators and Application Owners. On request, we enable it for all users.

- **Sign-in with your organization’s SSO (OIDC)**, which we recommend: the MFA and password policy of your own identity provider apply.
- **Sign-in with a local account** (e-mail and password): the second factor is an authenticator app (TOTP).

How setup and sign-in work is described in [Two-Factor Authentication](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/).

### [Which authenticator apps work for the second factor?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#which-authenticator-apps-work-for-the-second-factor)

Any app that implements TOTP, the open standard [RFC 6238](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6238), for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, FreeOTP, or password managers such as 1Password and Bitwarden. Sign-in runs on Keycloak, so its TOTP implementation applies; the [Keycloak documentation](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/#one-time-password-otp-policies) has the details.

TOTP is open and vendor-independent, needs no delivery channel, and has been in wide use since 2011, for example at Google, Microsoft, GitHub and AWS.

If a code is rejected, check that the device’s clock is set automatically. The app and the server both compute the code from the current time, so a clock that is off by more than a few seconds produces wrong codes.

### [Can the one-time code be sent by e-mail or SMS?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#can-the-one-time-code-be-sent-by-e-mail-or-sms)

No. Smartchat does not support e-mail or SMS as a second factor. Codes sent by e-mail or SMS are much weaker than an authenticator app: e-mails can be intercepted and are usually not encrypted, a mailbox can be taken over, and SMS is open to SIM swapping.

If your users cannot use an authenticator app, the alternatives are signing in through your organization’s SSO with its own MFA, or a custom procedure built for you as a separate project.

## [Spaces and groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#spaces-and-groups)

### [Should we use several Spaces?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#should-we-use-several-spaces)

Usually not. Work in one Space and model departments, teams and projects with groups. Several Spaces are only needed when data or administration must be strictly separated.

[Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/) are Smartchat’s tenant separation: data and permissions are completely isolated between them. They are meant for separate organizations, for example different legal entities of a group, such as T-Systems Brazil and T-Systems Germany. Most organizations are a single legal entity and need one Space.

More on this in [When to use several Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#when-to-use-several-spaces).

### [Should every department get its own Space?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#should-every-department-get-its-own-space)

No. Departments are what groups are for. Collections, assistants and prompt templates can be [shared with specific groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/), so only a department’s members see its data. Space Owners see every item unless the instance is set up to limit them, see [What Space Owners can see](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#what-space-owners-can-see).

Cross-department work, such as a project, is easy with groups: a user can belong to several groups, and the project gets a group of its own. With one Space per department this is not possible, because data from different Spaces cannot be used together.

### [How do we decide whether several Spaces make sense?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-do-we-decide-whether-several-spaces-make-sense)

Two questions help:

1. **Should a user work in several Spaces?** Then Spaces are not the right fit. A user only has access to the resources of the active Space and cannot access resources of several Spaces at the same time.
2. **Could a project or request need data from several Spaces?** Then Spaces are not the right fit. A chat or assistant only reaches data in the active Space.

It also helps to turn the question around: is it fine if every department has a group and only its members see the department’s data? If yes, one Space is enough.

### [When are several Spaces required?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#when-are-several-spaces-required)

Only when at least one of these applies:

- **Legal or compliance requirements** demand strict data separation.
- **Administrators must be strictly separated**, for example the admins of unit A must not manage the members of unit B. Within one Space, Space Owners manage all members, groups and content of that Space.

Even then, several Spaces are a trade-off that users feel in their daily work:

- Users have to know which Space they are in and where which data lives. Admins maintain members, groups and settings once per Space.
- Files, collections and assistants of one Space are not available in another.
- Moving data between Spaces is not a standard operation, only an exception.

We help you work out a roles and permissions concept that maps your organization to Spaces and groups before you decide.

## [Large document collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#large-document-collections)

### [Can Smartchat find and summarize information across millions or billions of documents?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#can-smartchat-find-and-summarize-information-across-millions-or-billions-of-documents)

Finding, yes. Once documents are indexed in [knowledge collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/), Smartchat searches millions of them quickly and passes the most relevant passages to the model. What is hard is having the model sift through all of them:

- **The model cannot read everything.** It takes in only a limited amount of text at once, see [How much content can the model use as context](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-much-content-can-the-model-use-as-context-and-can-it-be-limited). It summarizes the passages the search returns, not the whole archive.
- **The needle in the haystack.** If the answer is a single detail in one document among millions, the search has to find exactly that passage. That is a hard problem for any search system, and it gets harder the larger and more similar the documents are.

Indexing a whole archive of millions of documents is also a dedicated project with its own sizing and cost, because every document has to be processed and indexed. Two routes avoid that, and they can be combined:

- **Search at the source.** An agent uses the archive’s own search, through web search or an MCP server you connect, and retrieves only the relevant documents.
- **Two stages.** A stronger model with internet access searches the archive, selects documents and organises them, for example with summaries, into a knowledge collection. That collection is then used in a confidential setup with a model hosted by T-Systems and no internet access. [Deep Dive](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/) fits the second stage: it researches in several steps, uses only the attached collections, never the internet, and writes a report with sources.

## [Skills and knowledge](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#skills-and-knowledge)

### [Can users create reusable skills from their own knowledge and files?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#can-users-create-reusable-skills-from-their-own-knowledge-and-files)

- **Available today:** an assistant combines a model, fixed instructions and optionally knowledge collections. Assistants and prompt templates can be saved, shared and maintained together.
- **Agents:** agents can be specialised with skills, sets of instructions describing how to do a task, combined with the tools it needs. Skills can be stored in a shared library and controlled through access rights.
- **User-authored skills** are planned.

### [Where are the source files stored?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#where-are-the-source-files-stored)

Documents uploaded to collections, or synced from S3 or Confluence, are stored in your Smartchat environment in Germany. Files uploaded directly into a chat belong only to that chat.

### [How much content can the model use as context, and can it be limited?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-much-content-can-the-model-use-as-context-and-can-it-be-limited)

The model does not receive whole libraries. For each question, the most relevant passages are found and passed to the model. How much text a model can take in at once depends on the model, from about 100,000 tokens up to around 1 million. The context window of each model is listed in the [LLM Serving model documentation](https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/models/).

The context can be limited in three ways:

- Users choose which collections or files are attached to a chat or assistant.
- Administrators configure how documents are processed and searched.
- [Access control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/) decides which collections a user can see at all.

## [Models and capabilities](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#models-and-capabilities)

### [Which models are available, and how flexible is the selection?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#which-models-are-available-and-how-flexible-is-the-selection)

Smartchat offers models from T-Systems LLM Serving in two groups:

- **Models hosted by T-Systems in Germany**, available in all product variants.
- **Models from external providers** (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral AI), available in the Pro and Agentic variants and billed by actual token usage.

The Space Owner decides which models appear in their Space. Models are added and retired monthly. For the current list, see the [LLM Serving model documentation](https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/models/).

### [How does Smartchat compare with Microsoft Copilot?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/faq/#how-does-smartchat-compare-with-microsoft-copilot)

Microsoft 365 Copilot is closely tied to the Microsoft 365 ecosystem and its data (mail, Teams, SharePoint). Smartchat is independent of Microsoft 365. It offers a choice of models, including models hosted in Germany, and connects your own data sources and tools.

---

# Introduction

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/

> End-user introduction to Smartchat — what it is, how it works, and what it adds to OpenWebUI.

The T-Systems Smartchat is an AI chatbot application. Smartchat enables secure interaction with your own data sources using natural language. You can search documents for information, summarize their content, and generate new content or specific output formats based on them.

The technical foundation is a **Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)** architecture. RAG retrieves information from files or databases and provides it to the language model (Large Language Model, LLM) as context. This means chat responses are grounded in the retrieved content. Smartchat displays the name of each source used.

> **Data privacy**
>
> The language models used in Smartchat are **not** trained on user inputs. Data processing takes place in a secure cloud environment within the EU, operated by Telekom and hosted in T-Cloud Public. A [selection of LLMs](https://docs.llmhub.t-systems.net/plans/) is available and continuously updated with the latest models.
>
> Data you mark as [confidential](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/) is processed only by Telekom-hosted models and is never sent to external providers.

Smartchat is built on a fork of [OpenWebUI](https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui) combined with a custom multi-tenant Enterprise RAG framework, with content organized in isolated tenants called **Spaces**.

## [What Smartchat adds to OpenWebUI](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/#what-smartchat-adds-to-openwebui)

Multi-Tenancy

Fully isolated tenants (Spaces) with separate users, documents, and configurations — all on a single deployment.

Confidential Data

Mark a collection or a whole Space as confidential and Smartchat keeps it on Telekom-hosted models: no externally hosted models, no web search, no sharing.

Enterprise RBAC

[Roles, permissions and access control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/) per Space, synced with your SSO provider.

Async Ingestion Pipeline

Scalable, fully asynchronous document ingestion — handles large document volumes without blocking.

Security Hardening

Sandboxed code execution, input validation, and attack surface reduction beyond upstream defaults.

Compliance & Accessibility

Certified for enterprise compliance standards and accessibility requirements.

Confluence Integration

Connect Confluence Data Center spaces — pages are auto-synced and become searchable context in chats.

> **Disclaimer**
>
> Please note that this documentation covers only the generic features of Smartchat. Since the feature set provided is always individually defined in your contract, not all features described here may be part of your deployment.
>
> Additionally, custom features or role permissions may have been agreed upon that go beyond the standard scope of this documentation.

---

# Registration & Login

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/getting-started/

> Registration and login for Smartchat.

## [Registration & Login](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/getting-started/#registration--login)

If available, please log in using your company’s **Single Sign-On (SSO)**. Otherwise, follow the instructions below.

### [Registration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/getting-started/#registration)

Your account is created when an Application Owner or the Owner of your Space [adds you as a member](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/). You will receive an email with a verification link. Please check your email and use the “Forgot Password” option to create a new password. Your **new password** must contain **at least 16 characters**.

*\[Image: Registration confirmation email]*

*\[Image: Password update page]*

### [Login](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/getting-started/#login)

Open the login link provided in the welcome email you received. Then log in with your email address and password, or use your company SSO.

*\[Image: Login page]*

Depending on your installation, you may also be asked for a code from an authenticator app. See [Two-Factor Authentication](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/).

# Starting a Chat

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/

> Open a new chat, select a model, and make inputs.

## [Open a new chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#open-a-new-chat)

*\[Image: Chat window with "New Chat" button]*

Click **“New Chat”** in the left sidebar to start a new (empty) chat. In each chat, you can choose which of the available language models to use. In addition to a single model, you can also interact with two or more models simultaneously in a multi-model chat to compare their responses.

## [Select a model](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#select-a-model)

*\[Image: Model selection menu]*

Click the **dropdown menu** showing the currently selected model to switch models. Model names include visual indicators:

- **Logo** (before the name): If it shows the Telekom T, the model is hosted by Telekom. These models are the most secure (PSA DSK3-compliant for confidential data). Models without the T logo are externally hosted and cannot be used for confidential or internal documents. In a [confidential chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/), only models with the T logo are offered.
- **Country flag** (after the name): Indicates which country the model is hosted in.
- **Image icon** (after the flag): If the image is white, it is a multimodal model that can process images in addition to text.

Depending on your organization’s configuration, you may also have access to [assistants](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants).

## [Making inputs](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#making-inputs)

### [Writing manual prompts](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#writing-manual-prompts)

*\[Image: Prompt input in the chat window]*

A manual prompt is a directly written input in the chat interface. Type your query or instruction in the dialog window and send it using the arrow button or the Enter key.

### [Editing a prompt](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#editing-a-prompt)

*\[Image: Edit icon below the prompt]*

A prompt can be edited using the **pencil icon**. The response will be regenerated for the updated prompt. After editing, click “Send” to regenerate.

### [Speech to text](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#speech-to-text)

Instead of typing a prompt, you can dictate it: Smartchat converts the recording to text.

1. Click the **microphone** in the message box (**Record voice**) and start speaking.

   *\[Image: The microphone in the message box, with its tooltip Record voice]*

2. The first time, your browser asks whether Smartchat may use the microphone: allow it. If you blocked it before, allow it again in the browser’s site settings, which open from the icon next to the address bar.

   *\[Image: The browser’s site settings with the microphone permission set to Block]*

3. While you record, a timer shows the elapsed time against the maximum. Stop the recording to have it converted to text in the message box.

> **Recordings stop after about 10 minutes**
>
> A recording stops on its own at 9:50 and is transcribed as usual. For a longer dictation, record it in several parts.

### [Uploading files and screen captures](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/starting-a-chat/#uploading-files-and-screen-captures)

Uploading files allows you to interact directly with your own documents. This creates a private chat session between you, Smartchat, and the uploaded documents. Uploaded documents are not stored outside the chat.

> **Confidential documents**
>
> An uploaded file has no confidentiality flag of its own. To keep a document on Telekom-hosted models, add it to a [confidential collection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/) and attach the collection instead.

Use the **plus icon** in the chat window to upload files from your file manager or take screenshots of open applications. Files can also be dragged and dropped into a chat.

*\[Image: File upload menu]*

*\[Image: Screen capture dialog]*

---

# Working with Confidential Data

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/

> Step by step — create a confidential collection, chat with it, and see how Smartchat keeps confidential data on Telekom-hosted models.

Smartchat can keep confidential documents within Telekom-hosted infrastructure for you. This page walks through a typical example: a controlling team keeps the budget plan for 2027 in a confidential collection and asks questions about it. For the rules behind it, see [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/).

## [1. Create a confidential collection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#1-create-a-confidential-collection)

1. Open **Workspace → Collection** and click **Create Collection**.
2. Enter a name and a description.
3. Switch on **Confidential**. Hover over the label to see what it means.
4. Click **Create Collection**, then add your documents with the **+** button in the collection.

*\[Image: Create Collection form with the Confidential switch turned on]*

The collection now carries a shield in the collection list.

*\[Image: Collection list with the shield next to the confidential collection]*

To make an existing collection confidential, open it and switch on **Confidential** in its header. The change is saved right away.

*\[Image: Collection header with the Confidential switch]*

> **Tip**
>
> Put confidential documents into a confidential collection rather than uploading them straight into a chat. A file uploaded into a chat has no confidentiality flag of its own.

## [2. Use the collection in a chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#2-use-the-collection-in-a-chat)

In a new chat, type **#** and pick the collection. Confidential collections show the shield in the list.

*\[Image: Collection picker opened with # showing the confidential collection]*

As soon as the collection is attached, the chat is confidential. If an externally hosted model was selected, Smartchat switches to a Telekom-hosted model and tells you so.

*\[Image: Notification that the chat switched to a Telekom-hosted model]*

The shield icon next to the microphone shows that you are in a confidential chat.

*\[Image: Tooltip of the confidential chat icon in the chat input]*

## [3. What you can use in the chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#3-what-you-can-use-in-the-chat)

The model picker only offers models hosted by T-Systems. Externally hosted models are hidden.

*\[Image: Model picker showing only Telekom-hosted models and the confidential data note]*

Web search is greyed out in the **+** menu, because it would send parts of the conversation to an external search provider. Tools are not offered either.

*\[Image: Disabled web search entry in the + menu of a confidential chat]*

Ask your question as usual. The answer is generated by a Telekom-hosted model and cites the documents from your collection.

*\[Image: Answer from a Telekom-hosted model citing a document from the confidential collection]*

## [4. The chat stays confidential](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#4-the-chat-stays-confidential)

A confidential chat keeps its restrictions for its whole life:

- Removing the collection from the chat, or switching off **Confidential** on the collection later, does not lift them.
- **Share**, **Clone** and **Copy** are not offered in the chat menu, so the content stays within Smartchat. Export is still available.

If you need web search or an externally hosted model for a follow-up question, start a new chat without the confidential data.

## [Working in a confidential Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#working-in-a-confidential-space)

If your Space Owner has marked the whole Space as confidential, every chat in it is confidential from the start, with all the restrictions above. You do not have to mark individual collections.

When you open a confidential Space from a chat, Smartchat asks you to confirm first. **Continue** opens the Space and restricts the current chat to Telekom-hosted models for good; **Cancel** keeps you where you are.

*\[Image: Confirmation dialog: You selected a Confidential Space]*

## [Assistants with confidential collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/#assistants-with-confidential-collections)

An [assistant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants) that uses a confidential collection must run on a Telekom-hosted base model:

- When you attach a confidential collection in the assistant editor, the base model list only offers Telekom-hosted models. A previously chosen externally hosted base model is removed, and the editor tells you why.
- An existing assistant whose collection becomes confidential while it runs on an externally hosted model is shown as **Unavailable** in the model picker until you edit it and pick a Telekom-hosted base model.

Chats with such an assistant are confidential, just as if you had attached the collection yourself.

---

# Using Multiple Models Side by Side

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/multi-model/

> Multi-model chat and combining responses.

In each chat, you can choose which of the available language models to use. In addition to a single model, you can interact with two or more models simultaneously in a multi-model chat to compare and combine their responses.

## [Selecting multiple models](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/multi-model/#selecting-multiple-models)

*\[Image: Multi-model selection]*

Click the **plus button** next to the currently selected model to add an additional model. All inputs will now be answered by both models in parallel. This feature is useful for comparing different AI models, cross-checking responses, or gathering different ideas for a specific task.

## [Combining responses](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/multi-model/#combining-responses)

When using multiple models, responses can be merged into a single combined answer using the **branch icon** on the right side.

*\[Image: Merge icon with parallel responses]*

*\[Image: Combined response]*

# Understanding & Using Outputs

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/

> Viewing sources and applying functions to responses.

## [Viewing sources](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#viewing-sources)

When a space’s knowledge is used to generate a response, the response includes up to five references at the bottom. Click a source to view more details. Where a document has an original address, for example a Confluence page, the source links to that original; otherwise it links to the copy stored in Smartchat.

*\[Image: Response with source reference]*

The percentage next to each source indicates how strongly the document correlates with the generated response (relevance score):

- **High percentage (90%–100%)** — Most of the content can be derived almost exclusively from this document.
- **Medium percentage (50%–80%)** — The document contributes significantly but is only part of a composite answer.
- **Low percentage (below 50%)** — The document is only peripherally involved (supporting evidence, background knowledge).

The values are produced automatically by Smartchat’s retrieval and ranking mechanism: the semantic similarity between document content and response sections is measured and converted into a percentage relevance score.

*\[Image: Source detail view with relevance score]*

## [Functions on responses](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#functions-on-responses)

You can further interact with Smartchat responses: edit, copy, read aloud, continue, stop, or regenerate.

*\[Image: Function icons below a response]*

### [Edit response](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#edit-response)

*\[Image: Edit button]*

Click the **pencil icon** to edit a response. Use “Save as Copy” to save the output as a separate copy, or the Save button to overwrite.

*\[Image: Edit view with save options]*

### [Copy response](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#copy-response)

*\[Image: Copy button]*

Click the **copy icon** to copy the response to your clipboard.

### [Read response aloud](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#read-response-aloud)

*\[Image: Read aloud button]*

Click the **speaker icon** to have the response read aloud.

### [Continue/stop response](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#continuestop-response)

*\[Image: Continue button]*

Click the **play icon** to generate additional text.

*\[Image: Stop button during generation]*

An ongoing response can be interrupted using the **“Stop” icon** next to the text input.

### [Regenerate response](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/understanding-outputs/#regenerate-response)

*\[Image: Regenerate button]*

The **cycle icon** prompts the LLM to rephrase the response using different wording.

*\[Image: Regenerated response]*

# Rating Responses

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/

> Rate a response, share it with the owners of your Space, and withdraw your consent.

Below each response you can rate it with **Good Response** (thumbs up) or **Bad Response** (thumbs down). The owners of your Space use these ratings to see where Smartchat helps and where it falls short.

> **Note**
>
> The rating buttons only appear when feedback is switched on for your Space. Space Owners can turn it off.

## [Rating a response](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/#rating-a-response)

1. Click **Good Response** or **Bad Response** below the response.
2. Pick what you liked or what was wrong. A reason is required when you rate a response as bad.
3. Add a **Comment** if you like and click **Submit**.

The first time you rate a response, Smartchat asks for your consent before anything is shared. Click **Agree and submit** to share your rating.

## [What is shared](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/#what-is-shared)

The Space Owners of your Space and the Application Owners see:

- your rating and comment,
- the chat up to the rated response,
- your email address.

Your feedback is kept until it is deleted. If your instance deletes feedback automatically after a number of days, the rating card tells you so. To remove a single rating, open it again and click **Delete feedback**.

## [Withdrawing your consent](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/#withdrawing-your-consent)

Click **Revoke consent** in your settings under **General**, or in the rating card. This deletes all feedback you have shared, in every Space: every rating, category and comment. Space Owners and Application Owners can no longer see any of it, and the deletion cannot be undone.

The next time you rate a response, you are asked for your consent again.

# Managing & Organizing Chats

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/

> Search chat histories, create folders, pin, archive, and import chats.

## [Searching chat histories](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#searching-chat-histories)

*\[Image: Search bar in the chat overview]*

Use the **search bar** on the left side to search content from past chats and find old entries.

## [Organizing chats in folders](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#organizing-chats-in-folders)

*\[Image: New folder button]*

*\[Image: Folder context menu]*

Use the **plus button** in the chat overview to create folders for organizing and grouping chats. The three-dot menu lets you rename folders. Existing chats can be moved into folders via drag & drop.

## [Pinning, renaming, and managing chats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#pinning-renaming-and-managing-chats)

*\[Image: Chat context menu]*

Click the **three-dot icon** next to a chat to access the following actions:

- **Pin** — Pin the chat to the top of the list.
- **Rename** — Change the chat title.
- **Clone** — Create a copy of an existing chat.
- **Archive** — Remove from the overview without deleting. Can be [unarchived](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#unarchiving-chats) later.
- **Share** — Create a shareable link. Recipients can view and clone the chat, but not collaboratively edit it.
- **Move to folder**
- **Download** — Download the chat in various formats.
- **Delete** — Permanently remove the chat from the history (not recoverable).

> **Note**
>
> **Share** and **Clone** are not offered for [confidential chats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/), so their content stays within Smartchat.

Use the **tag icon** next to the three-dot menu to add **tags** (keywords) to chats for more efficient grouping across folders. You can also search for tags in the chat search bar.

## [Unarchiving chats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#unarchiving-chats)

Archived chats are no longer displayed in the chat overview. They can be restored via the **profile icon**.

*\[Image: Profile menu with "Archived Chats"]*

In this view, all archived chats can be restored individually (or all at once) or deleted. Archived chats can also be exported as a JSON file.

*\[Image: Archived chats dialog]*

## [Importing chats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#importing-chats)

Go to **Settings** under the profile icon and navigate to the “Chats” section.

*\[Image: Settings in the profile menu]*

Here you can import chats in JSON format.

*\[Image: Chat import in settings]*

# Workspaces & Collaboration

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/

> Understanding workspaces, setting permissions, creating knowledge collections and assistants.

> **See also**
>
> It is recommended to read the [Workspace](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/) concepts page first, to understand what a workspace is and how it relates to Spaces.

## [Navigating the workspace](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#navigating-the-workspace)

Open the workspace by clicking **“Workspace”** in the left sidebar.

*\[Image: Workspace button in navigation menu]*

The workspace is divided into tabs along the top bar: **Assistants**, **Knowledge**, **Prompts**. Each tab lets you create, edit, and configure the respective elements. Application Owners and Space Owners also see a **Connectors** tab, where they decide who in the Space may use each [connector](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/#choosing-who-can-use-a-connector).

*\[Image: Workspace with Assistants, Knowledge, Prompts tabs]*

## [Sharing](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#sharing)

Everything you create in the workspace starts as **Only you**. Click **Share** in the header of an item to share it with groups (**Can use** or **Can edit**) or with everyone in the Space. See [Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/).

## [Creating knowledge collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-knowledge-collections)

Local knowledge collections can be manually created, edited, and searched via the **“Knowledge”** tab. Existing knowledge collections can be referenced within a chat using the **hash key (#)**. Knowledge collections can also be attached as context to an assistant.

Switch on **Confidential** for a collection whose content must stay on Telekom-hosted models. Every chat that uses it becomes a confidential chat. See [Working with Confidential Data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/).

*\[Image: Knowledge collections in chat with # shortcut]*

## [Creating and using assistants](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants)

Assistants are configurations tailored to specific use cases. An existing LLM is enhanced with knowledge and a system prompt and shared within the organization, so it can be used for recurring tasks (e.g. summarizing emails and writing responses that comply with corporate guidelines).

Created assistants can be selected and used in the chat via the dropdown list like any other model.

*\[Image: Assistants tab in the workspace]*

In the **“Assistants”** tab, you can create and edit assistants:

- **Plus icon** — add a new assistant
- **Pencil icon** — edit an existing assistant
- **Toggle** — activate/deactivate an assistant in the dropdown list

Who can use an assistant in the chat and who can also edit it is decided when you [share](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/) it.

When creating an assistant, assign a **name**, **description**, and **base model**. The **system prompt** is the most powerful tool alongside the stored knowledge and defines the assistant’s general behavior. Knowledge collections must be created beforehand via the “Knowledge” tab. **Prompt suggestions** enable quick and intuitive usage.

An assistant that uses a [confidential collection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/) must run on a Telekom-hosted base model. Once a confidential collection is attached, the editor only offers those.

*\[Image: Assistant editing view]*

*\[Image: Additional assistant parameters: Tools, Filters, Actions, Capabilities]*

## [Creating and using prompt templates](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-prompt-templates)

Prompt templates are blueprints for prompts. They can be created and edited in the workspace under **“Prompts”**. Use the **plus icon** to add a new template. Like assistants and knowledge collections, you share them via **Share**.

Prompt templates have a **title** and the actual prompt content below. Variables for values to be filled in later are declared with curly braces, e.g. `Write an email to {{Name}}.` Built-in variables such as `{{CURRENT_DATE}}` fill themselves in, see [Prompt Variables](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/).

*\[Image: Plus button for new prompt template]*

*\[Image: Prompt template editing view]*

Existing templates can be invoked within a chat by typing the **forward slash (/)** and selecting the desired template from the dialog. Placeholders can then be filled with actual values.

> **Tip**
>
> Update multiple variable fields in sequence by pressing the Tab key in the input field after each entry.

*\[Image: Prompt template selection with / shortcut]*

# Customizing Smartchat

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/settings/

> Profile settings, chat dialog, and audio settings.

Open your personal settings for Smartchat and the interface via the **profile icon** in the top right.

*\[Image: General settings]*

## [General profile settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/settings/#general-profile-settings)

*\[Image: Interface and conversation settings]*

The general settings allow you to configure the user interface:

- **Theme** — Light/dark mode
- **Language**
- **Notifications** — enable/disable
- **Popup delay** — how long popup windows remain visible
- **General system prompt** — always active (e.g. “Always respond in bullet points.”)
- **Advanced parameters** — should only be adjusted when specifically needed

> **Changed in v3.19.0**
>
> In a chat with an assistant that has its own system prompt, your general system prompt is no longer used. Put instructions that must apply there into the assistant’s system prompt.

## [Customizing the chat dialog](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/settings/#customizing-the-chat-dialog)

*\[Image: Chat dialog settings]*

The interface settings let you configure the default parameters for the chat dialog. Options are grouped into **Interface**, **Conversation**, **Voice**, and **File**.

For example, under *Interface > Text direction* you can set whether text direction is left-to-right, right-to-left, or automatic.

## [Audio & speech settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/settings/#audio--speech-settings)

*\[Image: Audio settings]*

The audio settings let you configure audio input and output:

- **STT** (Speech-to-Text) — convert speech to text
- **TTS** (Text-to-Speech) — convert text to speech

# Deep Dive

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/

> How to use the Deep Dive research feature in Smartchat.

**Deep Dive** is Smartchat’s in-depth research mode, equivalent to what other AI chatbots call “Deep Research”. Instead of a single LLM response, Deep Dive runs a multi-step research agent that reads through your Space’s documents, synthesises findings, and writes a structured report complete with sources.

## [Requirements](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#requirements)

Space Users need the **Deep Dive** [permission](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/), set on one of their groups under **Space Owner → Groups**. Space Owners have it in their Space without a group.

## [How Deep Dive works](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#how-deep-dive-works)

### [Spaces only](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#spaces-only)

Deep Dive works inside a **Space**. It searches all documents in the Space you currently have open. You cannot restrict which documents it uses; it always searches the full Space knowledge base. If you need answers from a different knowledge base, switch to that Space before starting a run.

### [Your settings are set aside](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#your-settings-are-set-aside)

Model selection, reasoning effort, and any system prompt configured for the Space do not affect a Deep Dive run. The agent uses its own dedicated research model to ensure consistent, reliable results. That research model is always a T-Cloud model hosted by T-Systems, so Deep Dive can be used with [confidential](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/) data: all processing takes place in Germany and no data is sent to an external party. Only your direct research question influences what it does. Nothing changes for your regular chat.

## [How often can I use it?](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#how-often-can-i-use-it)

Each user has:

- **10 runs per day**: the toggle shows how many you have used out of your daily total (e.g. `0/10`).
- **2 concurrent runs**: you can have up to two Deep Dive runs active at the same time across all your chats.

Daily runs reset at midnight.

Individual agreements can override these limits, so your own limit may be different. Application Owners are exempt from them entirely.

## [Starting a Deep Dive](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#starting-a-deep-dive)

*\[Image: Deep Dive toggle in the message input showing remaining daily runs]*

1. Open the Space whose documents you want the agent to research.
2. Toggle **Deep Dive** in the message input area before sending your message. The toggle shows how many runs you have used today.
3. Type your research question and send it.

## [Approving the research plan](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#approving-the-research-plan)

After receiving your question, Deep Dive proposes a refined research question for your review before doing any work. The status indicator shows **“Awaiting approval”**. You have three options:

*\[Image: Research question proposal with Approve, Give Feedback, and Reject buttons and "Awaiting approval" status]*

| Action | What happens |
| - | - |
| **Approve** | The agent starts working immediately. |
| **Give Feedback** | Opens a text field where you can describe what to change. The agent revises the research question and asks again. |
| **Reject** | Cancels the run. No quota is consumed. |

The agent will not start working until you approve. If you close the chat while it is awaiting approval, the run stays paused until you return and respond.

## [While the agent is running](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#while-the-agent-is-running)

Once approved, the agent runs in the background. You will see:

*\[Image: Agent streaming live updates into the chat with "Working" status]*

- A **spinner** in the bottom-right corner of the chat.
- The status indicator in the top-right corner of the agent message showing **“Working”**.
- Live updates streamed into the chat as the agent works, including documents it finds along the way.

You can close the chat or switch to a different chat and the agent will keep running. Come back to the same chat to see the final report when it is done.

## [The research report](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/#the-research-report)

When the run completes, the status changes to **“Completed”** and the agent delivers its findings as a formatted Markdown report with:

*\[Image: Completed Deep Dive with "Deep Dive Event History" and "Open Report" button]*

- **Inline citations**: every claim links back to the source document.
- **Downloadable report**: export the full report as a file.

The report is added to the chat history like a regular message. You can ask follow-up questions in the same chat afterwards. Follow-ups use regular chat mode and will not trigger another Deep Dive run unless you toggle Deep Dive again.

---

# Prompt Variables

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/

> Placeholders such as today's date or your name that fill themselves in when you use a prompt template or your personal system prompt.

**Prompt variables** are placeholders in double curly braces, such as `{{CURRENT_DATE}}`. Smartchat replaces them with a current value, so a [prompt template](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-prompt-templates) or your personal system prompt stays up to date without editing.

## [Available variables](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/#available-variables)

| Variable | Replaced with | Prompt templates | Personal system prompt |
| - | - | :-: | :-: |
| `{{CURRENT_DATE}}` | Today’s date, e.g. `2026-11-04` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{CURRENT_TIME}}` | The current time, e.g. `14:05:09` (system prompt: `2:05:09 PM`) | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{CURRENT_DATETIME}}` | Date and time combined | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{CURRENT_WEEKDAY}}` | The weekday in English, e.g. `Wednesday` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{CURRENT_TIMEZONE}}` | Your time zone, e.g. `Europe/Berlin` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{USER_NAME}}` | Your display name | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{USER_LANGUAGE}}` | Your interface language, e.g. `de-DE` | ✓ | ✓ |
| `{{USER_LOCATION}}` | Your coordinates, if you allow location access in your browser | ✓ | – |
| `{{CLIPBOARD}}` | The text in your clipboard | ✓ | – |

Date, time and time zone are taken from your device. Variables must be written exactly as shown, in capital letters.

## [Variables in prompt templates](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/#variables-in-prompt-templates)

1. Open **Workspace → Prompts** and create a new prompt template or open an existing one.
2. Write the variables into the prompt content. Any other word in double curly braces, such as `{{recipient}}`, is a gap that you fill in yourself each time you use the template.
3. In the chat, type **/** followed by the template’s command and select the template.

The variables are filled in as soon as you select the template, and the text appears in the chat input. The first gap is selected, so you can type over it. Press **Tab** to jump to the next gap. Check the text, then send it.

Example template:

```text
Write a short status update for {{recipient}} as of {{CURRENT_DATE}}. Sign it with {{USER_NAME}}.
```

> **Note**
>
> - A gap you do not fill in is sent to the model as written, including the curly braces.
> - For `{{CLIPBOARD}}` and `{{USER_LOCATION}}`, your browser may ask for permission. If you copied an image, it is attached to the message as well.

## [Variables in your personal system prompt](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/#variables-in-your-personal-system-prompt)

Variables also work in your personal system prompt under **Settings → General → System Prompt (Advanced)**. They are filled in each time you send a message, so the model always sees the current values.

> **Caution**
>
> In the personal system prompt, each variable is only replaced the first time it appears. Use every variable at most once.

Gaps such as `{{recipient}}`, `{{CLIPBOARD}}` and `{{USER_LOCATION}}` are not filled in here.

## [Where variables are not replaced](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/prompt-variables/#where-variables-are-not-replaced)

- **Assistant system prompts:** the system prompt of an [Assistant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants) is sent to the model exactly as written. Variables in it stay unchanged.
- **Prompt suggestions** on the start screen: only `{{CLIPBOARD}}` is filled in.

> **Tip**
>
> Smartchat tells the model today’s date in every chat. You do not need `{{CURRENT_DATE}}` just so the model knows the date.

---

# Reasoning Effort

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/reasoning-effort/

> Choose how much a reasoning model thinks before it answers.

Some models think a question through before they answer. **Reasoning effort** sets how much thinking they may do: more effort usually gives better answers to hard questions, such as analyses, calculations or code, but the answer takes longer and uses more tokens.

## [Choosing the effort](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/reasoning-effort/#choosing-the-effort)

The selector shows the chosen effort, here Default.

1. Select a model that supports reasoning effort. A selector then appears in the message box that shows the current effort, for example **Default**. It only appears when every selected model supports reasoning effort, and disappears again when you add a model that does not.
2. Open it and pick **Low**, **Medium** or **High**.
3. Send your message. The effort applies to the messages you send until you change it.

Depending on the model, the list also offers a first option that leaves the effort to the model: **Default**, **Auto**, or **Disabled** for models that then answer without thinking first.

> **When to raise it**
>
> Start with the model’s default. Raise the effort when an answer to a demanding question misses steps or gets details wrong, and lower it for quick questions where speed matters more.

Reasoning effort does not apply to [Deep Dive](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/deep-dive/), which decides how long it researches by itself.

---

# Web Search

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/

> Give Smartchat access to live web results via an external search provider or your model's built-in capability.

Smartchat supports two ways to bring live web results into a conversation:

- **Web Search**: Smartchat queries an external search provider (Bing, Brave, Google, etc.) and injects the results into context. Works with any model; requires prior setup by T-Systems.
- **Native Web Search**: The model provider performs the search as a built-in capability. Available for Google (Gemini) and Anthropic (Claude) models only.

Both types are gated behind the same **Web Search** feature permission. Once a type is available, it is on in every Space, and a Space Owner can switch it off for their Space.

## [Web Search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#web-search)

Web Search works with every model, regardless of provider. Smartchat queries a configured external search provider and passes the results to the model as context. No LLM provider tool support is needed.

This is an opt-in feature: it is only available when a Space Owner has switched it on for the Space and a search provider API key is configured.

### [Supported Search Providers](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#supported-search-providers)

All [OpenWebUI-compatible search providers](https://docs.openwebui.com/category/web-search) are supported, including Bing, Brave, Google, Jina, Kagi, Mojeek, Perplexity, and others.

### [Setup by the Space Owner](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#setup-by-the-space-owner)

1. Click your profile image and choose **Administration**.
2. Go to **Space Owner → Web Search** and check that the right Space is shown in **Selected Space**.
3. Once web search is set up for your environment, **Web Search** is on in every Space. Switch it off to take web search away from the Space’s users, and back on to return it.
4. Select a **Web Search Engine** from the dropdown.

## [Native Web Search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#native-web-search)

Native web search uses the model provider’s built-in search capability. No separate search provider account or API key is needed. It works out of the box in Smartchat for anyone who has access to a supported model.

### [Supported Providers](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#supported-providers)

- **Google** (Gemini)
- **Anthropic** (Claude)

In the model picker, models that support native web search are indicated with a **Globe icon** (🌐).

> **Not available for T-Cloud models**
>
> Native web search is a capability of the model provider, so it does **not** work with the open source models hosted by T-Systems in the T-Cloud. To use web search with those models, use the regular [Web Search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#web-search) above, which requires a separate search provider license.

### [Setup by the Space Owner](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#setup-by-the-space-owner-1)

1. Click your profile image and choose **Administration**.
2. Go to **Space Owner → Web Search** and check that the right Space is shown in **Selected Space**.
3. **Enable Native Web Search** is on in every Space. Switch it off to take native web search away from the Space’s users, and back on to return it.

## [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#permissions)

Space Owners have every [permission](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/) of their Space, so they need no group. Other members need the **Web Search** permission, through one of their [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) or the Space’s default permissions. It is off by default.

To grant the permission:

1. In Administration, go to **Space Owner → Groups**.
2. Click on a group, or click **Default permissions** to grant the permission to every member of the Space. Only Application Owners see **Default permissions**.
3. Open the **Permissions** tab.
4. Under **Features Permissions**, enable **Web Search**.

Web search must also be switched on for your Smartchat instance. If it is off there, nobody can use it, Space Owners included. See [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/).

## [Using Web Search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#using-web-search)

**Web Search (external provider):** Available for any model once a Space Owner has switched it on. To use it, enable the **Web Search** toggle in the prompt window, then send your prompt. Smartchat fetches relevant results and provides them to the model.

**Native Web Search:** Open a chat and, from the model picker, select a model marked with the Globe icon (🌐). Enable the **Web Search** toggle in the prompt window, then send your prompt. The model fetches live web results and incorporates them into its response.

**When both are available:** If Web Search (external provider) is configured for your environment and you select a model that also supports native web search, you can choose which type to use on a per-message basis in the chat interface. Results may differ between the two types depending on the search provider and the model’s built-in search capability.

## [Combining Web Search with Your Data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#combining-web-search-with-your-data)

Web search can be used together with your own data in the same chat — collections as well as files you upload — as long as that data is **not confidential**. Confidentiality is what governs the combination, not the kind of data:

- **Non-confidential collections, Spaces, and uploaded files** can be combined with web search.
- **Confidential collections or Spaces** cannot be combined with web search. If a collection or its Space is marked as confidential, web search is unavailable in that chat.
- **Files from a confidential collection** behave the same way: attaching one makes the chat confidential, so web search is unavailable in it.

Web search sends parts of the conversation to an external provider, so it must never be used with confidential data. Users must be aware that enabling web search in a chat involving confidential information poses a data security risk and must be avoided. This can be enforced at two levels: any user can mark a collection as confidential, and admins can mark Spaces as confidential. See [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/) for details on how the confidentiality flag works.

## [See also](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/#see-also)

- [Tiers & Features](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/features/v2-feature-overview)
- [Release Notes](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/release-notes/)

---

# Confidentiality

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/

> How Smartchat keeps confidential data inside Telekom-hosted infrastructure, and what changes when a collection, a Space or a chat is confidential.

**Confidentiality** is Smartchat’s built-in protection for data that must not leave the secure Smartchat environment. Once data is marked confidential, Smartchat enforces the rules for you: confidential data is only ever processed by models hosted by T-Systems, and every feature that would send it to an external system is switched off. You do not need to remember which model or feature is safe to use.

> **In short**
>
> - Mark a **collection** or a whole **Space** as confidential.
> - Every chat that uses that data becomes a **confidential chat**, and stays one.
> - A confidential chat only uses Telekom-hosted models (Telekom **T** logo), and web search, tools and sharing are unavailable in it.

For a step-by-step walkthrough with screenshots, see [Working with Confidential Data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/confidential-data/).

## [Where confidentiality is set](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#where-confidentiality-is-set)

### [Confidential collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#confidential-collections)

Every [collection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-knowledge-collections) has a **Confidential** switch, off by default. Switch it on when you create the collection, or later in the collection’s header. Anyone who can edit the collection can change it.

*\[Image: Collection header with the Confidential switch turned on]*

Files have no confidentiality flag of their own: a file is confidential because it belongs to a confidential collection. A file you upload directly into a chat is not confidential by itself.

> **Keep confidential documents in a confidential collection**
>
> To protect a document, add it to a confidential collection and use the collection in your chats. A document uploaded straight into a chat is only protected if the chat is already confidential, for example because its Space is confidential.

### [Confidential Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#confidential-spaces)

A Space Owner or an Application Owner can mark a whole [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/) as confidential with the **Confidential Data** switch (see [Space Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#confidential-data)). All data in that Space is then treated as confidential, regardless of the setting of each collection. The Space setting can only add protection: it makes every collection in the Space confidential, but never makes a confidential collection non-confidential.

Your personal **My Space** cannot be marked confidential. There, confidentiality comes from the collections you use.

### [Confidential chats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#confidential-chats)

A chat becomes confidential as soon as:

- its Space is confidential,
- you attach a confidential collection, or a file from one, or
- you pick an [assistant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants) that uses a confidential collection.

Smartchat applies the restrictions the moment you attach the data, before you send your message. Once a chat is confidential it **stays confidential**, even if you remove the attachment again or the collection is no longer marked confidential later. To work without the restrictions, start a new chat without the confidential data.

*\[Image: Chat input with an attached confidential collection and the confidential chat icon]*

## [How to recognise confidential data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#how-to-recognise-confidential-data)

Confidential data is marked with a **shield** icon wherever it appears.

| Where | What you see |
| - | - |
| Workspace → **Collection** | A shield next to every confidential collection; a **Confidential** switch in the collection header. |
| **#** collection picker in the chat | A shield next to confidential collections. |
| Attachments in the chat input and in sent messages | A shield on every confidential collection or file. |
| Chat input | A shield icon next to the microphone. Hover over it for *“Confidential chat: only Telekom hosted models are available to prevent sending your data to external providers.”* |
| Model picker | Only the **Telekom hosted** models, with the note *“Confidential data: only Telekom-hosted models available.”* |
| Space selector | A confirmation dialog when you open a confidential Space from a chat. |

## [What changes in a confidential chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#what-changes-in-a-confidential-chat)

| Feature | In a confidential chat |
| - | - |
| **Models** | Only models hosted by T-Systems are available. Externally hosted models are hidden from the model picker. If an externally hosted model was selected, Smartchat switches to a Telekom-hosted one and tells you: *“Switched to a Telekom-hosted model due to confidentiality restrictions.”* Adding a second model with **@** is not available. |
| **Assistants** | An assistant that uses a confidential collection must be built on a Telekom-hosted base model. Otherwise it is shown as unavailable and cannot be selected. |
| **[Web search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/web-search/)** | Unavailable: *“Web search is not available in confidential chats”*. Web search sends parts of the conversation to an external search provider. |
| **Tools** | Unavailable, because tools can pass data on to external systems. |
| **[Share, Clone, Copy](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/managing-chats/#pinning-renaming-and-managing-chats)** | Not offered, so the content cannot be passed on outside Smartchat. |
| **Export** | Still available. An exported file is in your hands; handle it according to your organisation’s rules for confidential data. |

Smartchat enforces the model and web search restrictions on the server as well. A request that tries to use an externally hosted model in a confidential chat is rejected, the model is switched, and Smartchat asks you to send your message again.

Future features that transmit data to external systems will be guarded by the same mechanism.

## [Who can set it](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#who-can-set-it)

| Level | Who | Where |
| - | - | - |
| Collection | Anyone who can [edit](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/) the collection | Workspace → **Collection** → the collection → **Confidential** |
| Space | Space Owner | **Administration → Space Owner → Space → Confidential Data** ([Space Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#confidential-data)) |
| Space | Application Owner | **Administration → Application Owner → Spaces** ([Application Owner](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/)) |

Both switches can be turned off again. Chats that are already confidential stay confidential.

## [Why this matters](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#why-this-matters)

Models hosted by T-Systems in the T-Cloud (indicated by the Telekom **T** logo in the model picker) process data within the secure environment and are approved for confidential data ([PSA DSK3-compliant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/glossary/)). Externally hosted models, web search and similar features route data through the infrastructure of external providers. Confidentiality ensures that data requiring the highest level of protection stays within the secure boundary, without relying on every user to make the right choice every time.

---

# Roles, Permissions & Access Control

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/

> How roles, permissions and access control differ, and how groups connect them.

Roles, permissions and access control each decide something different. Each concept has its own page:

| Concept | Decides | Applies to |
| - | - | - |
| **[Roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/)** | Who administers Smartchat and its Spaces: members, groups and settings | The whole instance or one Space |
| **[Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/)** | Which features Space Users can use and which actions they can take, such as using web search or building agents | One Space |
| **[Access control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/)** | Who can use or edit an item, such as a collection or an agent | A single item |

What a role allows cannot be changed per person. Permissions only concern Space Users, because Space Owners have every permission of their Space through their role.

[Groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) connect permissions and access control: permissions are set on groups, and items are shared with groups.

---

# Roles

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/

> The roles in Smartchat (Application Owner, Data Scientist, Space Owner, Space User) and what each of them can administer.

Every member of a Space starts there with the **Space User** role: they can use the Space’s chat, its features and the items shared with them. Further roles add administrative tasks, such as adding members, creating groups or changing a Space’s settings. Roles exist on two levels:

- **Global roles** apply to the whole Smartchat instance.
- **Space roles** apply to one Space. You hold a separate Space role in each Space you belong to, so you can be a Space Owner in one Space and a Space User in another.

How roles, permissions and access control differ is explained in [Roles, Permissions & Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/).

## [Global roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/#global-roles)

The global roles are independent of each other: a user may hold either, both or neither.

- **Application Owner:** the top-level administrator of the instance, working in [**Administration → Application Owner**](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/).
- **Data Scientist:** manages the ingest and retrieval configuration of the whole instance.

| Capability | Application Owner | Data Scientist |
| - | :-: | :-: |
| Assign the global Data Scientist role | ✅ | ❌ |
| View statistics across all Spaces | ✅ | ❌ |
| [Manage all Spaces and users](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/) of the instance | ✅ | ❌ |
| Manage settings that apply to the whole instance (**Interface**, **Code Execution**) | ✅ | ❌ |
| Manage global ingest & retrieval configuration (embedding models, pipelines) | ❌ | ✅ |

## [Space roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/#space-roles)

- **Space User:** the role every member starts with. The Space appears in their Space selector.
- **Space Owner:** an administrator of the Space, working in [**Administration → Space Owner**](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/). A Space can have several Space Owners. A Space Owner has everything a Space User has, plus the administrative tasks below.

| Capability | Space User | Space Owner | Application Owner |
| - | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Create or delete the Space | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |
| [Add or remove Space members](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| [Promote or demote Space Owners](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#changing-a-members-role) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Set the Space’s confidentiality and API key | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| [Manage the other Space settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/) (e.g. LLMs) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅\* |
| Set up [Confluence sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/) and [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅\* |
| Choose which [connectors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/#choosing-who-can-use-a-connector) the members may use | ❌ | ✅ | ✅\* |
| Manage [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) and their [permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/) | ❌ | ✅ | ✅\* |

\* Only in Spaces where they also hold a Space role. The Space User role is enough.

> **Note**
>
> - A Space Owner’s tasks apply within their **own** Space. An Application Owner creates, deletes and staffs **any** Space.
> - A Space Owner cannot demote themselves; at least one Space Owner must remain per Space.
> - To work in a Space, an Application Owner gives themselves a Space role there like any other user.
> - Files and roles in a Space belong to the Space, not to the Space Owner who created them. They remain when that Space Owner’s account is deleted.

---

# Groups

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/

> The groups every Space has, who manages them, and how to create one.

Groups are the central tool for access and permission control in a [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/). They do two jobs:

- **Sharing:** collections, assistants, prompts and agents can be shared with a group, so that its members can use or edit them. See [Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/).
- **Permissions:** a group can allow its members to use features, for example building agents, web search, or sharing items with everyone in the Space. See [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/).
