Every group belongs to one Space and has no effect in any other Space. How roles, permissions and access control differ is explained in [Roles, Permissions & Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/).

Ben is in Sales and in the project group, so he gets both: he can use Web Search and build agents, use the Sales playbook and edit the Supplier portal docs. Everyone in the Space can use Acme - General. Carla’s draft prompt is private: she has not shared it with any group.

## [Groups every Space has](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/#groups-every-space-has)

Smartchat creates two groups in every Space and keeps their members up to date:

- **SpaceOwners {Space}** contains the Space Owners of the Space. Nothing about this group can be changed.
- **Users {Space}** contains every member of the Space. Only its permissions can be changed.

Sharing an item with **Everyone in this space** gives the **Users** group access. Permissions set on the **Users** group apply to every member of the Space.

## [Who manages groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/#who-manages-groups)

Space Owners manage the groups of their Space under **Administration → Space Owner → Groups**. They create and delete groups, add and remove members, and set each group’s permissions.

Two permissions let other members manage groups as well:

- **Group Management**, under **Danger Zone**: manage every group in the Space, like a Space Owner. Anyone who has it can also grant it to others.
- **Own Group Management**, under **Workspace Permissions**: create groups and manage the members of the groups you created, without changing their permissions.

## [Creating a group](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/#creating-a-group)

1. Click your profile image and choose **Administration**.
2. Go to **Space Owner → Groups**, check that the right Space is selected, and click **Add Group**.
3. Enter a name, optionally a description, and click **Create**.
4. Open the group. Add its members on the **Users** tab and set its [permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/) on the **Permissions** tab.

A new group starts empty:

- It has no members, not even you.
- Nothing is shared with it.
- Its permissions are the Space’s [default permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#default-permissions) at the time it is created.

If your Smartchat signs in through your organization’s identity provider, a group can also list **Identity provider group attributes**. Users whose identity provider group matches are added to the group when they sign in.

When someone is removed from the Space, they are removed from all of its groups.

---

# Permissions

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/

> What permissions allow, where they are set, and how they combine.

Which items a member of a [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/) can access is decided by [access control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/). Permissions decide which features they can use and which actions they can take in the Space, such as using web search, building agents, uploading files to chats or sharing items with everyone in the Space.

How roles, permissions and access control differ is explained in [Roles, Permissions & Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/).

The Space’s [default permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#default-permissions) decide which permissions a new [group](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) starts with. Permissions apply only in their Space.

## [All permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#all-permissions)

The **Permissions** tab of a group has these permissions. The **Default** column shows the value in a new Space.

| Permission | Allows | Default |
| - | - | - |
| **Workspace Permissions** | | |
| **Model Management** | Creating assistants | Off |
| **Collection Management** | Creating collections | Off |
| **Prompt Management** | Creating prompts | Off |
| **Agent Management**\* | Building agents | Off |
| **Own Group Management** | Creating groups and managing the members of groups you created | Off |
| **Sharing Permissions** | | |
| **Models Public Sharing** | Sharing assistants with everyone in the Space | Off |
| **Knowledge Public Sharing** | Sharing collections with everyone in the Space | Off |
| **Prompts Public Sharing** | Sharing prompts with everyone in the Space | Off |
| **Agents Public Sharing**\* | Sharing agents with everyone in the Space | Off |
| **Chat Permissions** | | |
| **Allow File Upload** | Attaching files to chat messages | On |
| **Allow Chat Controls**\* | Opening the chat controls, such as the system prompt and model parameters | Off |
| **Allow Speech to Text** | Dictating messages by voice | On |
| **Allow Text to Speech** | Having answers read aloud | On |
| **User Feedback**\* | Giving feedback on answers | Off |
| **Allow Multiple Models in Chat** | Using several models side by side in one chat | On |
| **Allow Temporary Chat** | Having chats that are not saved | On |
| **Features Permissions** | | |
| **Deep Dive**\* | Using Deep Dive | Off |
| **Web Search**\* | Using web search | Off |
| **Danger Zone** | | |
| **Group Management** | Managing every group in the Space, like a Space Owner | Off |

\* Only appears where the feature is available in your Smartchat.

Deleting and editing your own chats needs no permission: every member can always do both.

## [Rules](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#rules)

Rules restrict what members can do, instead of allowing something.

- **Enforce Temporary Chat:** every chat of the group’s members is temporary and is not saved. Space Owners are exempt.

## [Default permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#default-permissions)

Besides its groups, every Space has **Default permissions** that apply to all of its members. They are under **Space Owner → Groups → Default permissions**.

> **Application Owners only**
>
> Only Application Owners can see and change the default permissions. Space Owners cannot, not even in their own Space.

In a new Space, the values from the **Default** column under [All permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#all-permissions) apply.

A new group starts with the default permissions that apply when it is created. Groups that already exist keep their own settings: if a permission is on in an existing group, its members keep it after the default is switched off.

## [How permissions combine](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#how-permissions-combine)

A permission is on for you if it is on in the Space’s default permissions or in at least one of your groups. A group can only grant a permission, never take away one that another group grants.

Ben is in the groups Users, Sales and Project. A permission is on for him as soon as the defaults or one of his groups have it on: he gets Web Search through Sales. The Project group has file upload off, but that does not take it away, because it is on in the defaults. Deep Dive is on nowhere, so it is off for him too.

Only your groups in the active Space count.

## [Space Owners](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#space-owners)

Space Owners have every permission of their Space, without being in a group.

---

# Access Control

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/

> Who can use and edit the items in a Space, how to share them, and what Space Owners can see.

Access control decides who can use and edit a [workspace item](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/): a collection, assistant, prompt or agent. Items are shared with [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/), not with individual people. Like groups and permissions, access control always applies within one [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#scope) only.

How roles, permissions and access control differ is explained in [Roles, Permissions & Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles-permissions-access-control/).

## [Private by default](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#private-by-default)

> **Note**
>
> Everything you create in the workspace starts as **Only you**: nobody else can see it until you share it with a group or with everyone in the Space. Depending on a setting, Space Owners are an exception, see [What Space Owners can see](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#what-space-owners-can-see).
>
> **This does not apply to chats:** nobody but you sees your chats, not even a Space Owner.

The **{Space} - General** collection is the only item that every member can use from the start. Only Space Owners can edit it.

## [Who can access an item](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#who-can-access-an-item)

Click **Share** in the header of an item to open its share dialog. Under **Who can access**, choose one of four options:

| Option | Who can use it | Who can edit it |
| - | - | - |
| **Only you** | You | You |
| **Specific groups** | You and the groups you add | You and the groups set to **Can edit** |
| **Everyone can use** | Every member of the Space | You and the groups under **Groups that can also edit** |
| **Everyone can use & edit** | Every member of the Space | Every member of the Space |

A prompt shared with two groups: Sales can use it, Project: Supplier portal can also edit it.

**Can use** means finding the item and using it in chats, for example the files of a collection or an assistant to chat with. **Can edit** also allows changing it, for example adding files to a collection or changing an agent’s instructions and tools.

“Everyone” means the members of the active Space. In the list of groups, they appear as **Everyone in this space**.

If you are in several groups, their access adds up: if one of your groups can use an item and another can edit it, you can edit it.

## [Who can share](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#who-can-share)

- **With specific groups:** anyone who owns an item. Space Users can only add groups they belong to; Space Owners can add any group of the Space.
- **With everyone in the Space:** only members who have the matching **Public Sharing** permission, see [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/).

## [Who can change sharing](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#who-can-change-sharing)

> **Changed in v3.15.1**
>
> Only an item’s owner, Space Owners and Application Owners can change who has access to an item or delete it. A group that can edit the item can change its content, but sees its share dialog read-only.

## [What Space Owners can see](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#what-space-owners-can-see)

What Space Owners see in the workspace of their Space depends on a setting. There are two options:

- **Space Owners see every item (default).** They see every collection, assistant, prompt and agent in the workspace of their Space, including items set to **Only you**, and can edit and share them.
- **Space Owners only see what is shared with them.** Like every other member, they see their own items and items shared with their groups or with everyone.

The setting applies to the whole Smartchat instance, not to a single Space, and to Application Owners just as to Space Owners. Ask your Smartchat contact to turn on the second option.

Space Owners never see other members’ chats.

Space Owners manage the Space either way: its members, groups and settings. They also have every permission of their Space, see [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#space-owners).

## [Scope](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/#scope)

Access is always limited to the active Space:

- You can only share with groups of the current Space.
- A shared item is only visible inside that Space. It cannot be used from another Space, even by someone who is a member of both.
- Groups belong to one Space, so a group named `engineering` in Space A is unrelated to a group of the same name in Space B.

---

# Two-Factor Authentication

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/

> How two-factor authentication works when you log in to Smartchat with email and password, and how the authenticator app relates to the login.

Logins with email and password are handled by [Keycloak](https://www.keycloak.org/), the identity and access management system behind Smartchat. Keycloak can ask for a **second factor** after the password: a one-time code from an authenticator app on your phone. Whether this is required, and for whom, depends on how your installation is configured.

> **Single Sign-On**
>
> If you log in with your company’s **SSO**, your company’s identity provider handles authentication, including any second factor. This page applies to logins with email and password.

## [Authenticator apps](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/#authenticator-apps)

Any app that generates time-based one-time passwords (TOTP, [RFC 6238](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6238)) works, for example FreeOTP, Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, or a password manager with TOTP support.

## [Setting it up](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/#setting-it-up)

When two-factor authentication is required for your account, Keycloak asks you to set it up at your next login:

1. Scan the QR code shown on the login page with your authenticator app.
2. Enter the 6-digit code the app now shows, and optionally give the device a name.

From then on, every login asks for the current code from the app after your password. If you lose access to your phone, contact your administrator, who can have you set up a new authenticator app.

## [How the app and Smartchat communicate](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/#how-the-app-and-smartchat-communicate)

**They don’t.** The authenticator app never connects to Smartchat or Keycloak, and Keycloak never sends anything to the app. Both sides compute the same codes independently:

*\[Image: Diagram]*

- **Setup:** Keycloak generates a random secret for your account and shows it as a QR code on the login page, which is delivered over HTTPS. The app reads the QR code through the camera and stores the secret on the phone. This is the only time the secret leaves Keycloak.
- **Login:** every 30 seconds, the app and Keycloak each derive a new code from the shared secret and the current time. You type the app’s code into the login page, and it is sent to Keycloak over HTTPS like the rest of the login form.

The app therefore works offline and sends no data of its own. Its clock must be roughly correct. Keycloak accepts the codes of neighbouring time intervals to absorb small clock differences ([look-around window](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#totp-configuration-options)).

## [For administrators](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/two-factor-authentication/#for-administrators)

Two-factor authentication is part of the Keycloak login flow of your installation. Depending on the configuration it is:

- required for every login with email and password,
- required only for users with a specific role, or
- asked only from users who have already set up an authenticator app.

Keycloak documents the building blocks:

- [OTP policies](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#one-time-password-otp-policies): algorithm, number of digits and code period. The standard configuration uses Keycloak’s defaults, which every common authenticator app supports.
- [Conditions in conditional flows](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#conditions-in-conditional-flows) and [2FA conditional workflow examples](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#twofa-conditional-workflow-examples): how the second factor is required for all users, by role, or only once configured.
- [Required actions](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#proc-setting-required-actions_server_administration_guide): how a user is asked to set up an authenticator app at the next login.
- [Creating an OTP](https://www.keycloak.org/docs/latest/server_admin/index.html#proc_creating-otp_server_administration_guide): how to make a user set up a new authenticator app, for example after losing their phone.

---

# Spaces

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/

> How Spaces work — Smartchat's multi-tenancy boundary.

A **Space** is Smartchat’s multi-tenancy boundary. Every resource lives inside exactly one Space, and resources are completely isolated between Spaces — an entity in one Space cannot be accessed from another, not even by the same user who owns it.

> **Several Spaces are a deliberate decision**
>
> Do not create one Space per department. A common pattern is to start with a Space per department, then find that teams work across departments, in projects or shared requests. Spaces cannot support that, and by then changing it takes effort.
>
> Always try working with [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) *within* one Space first. For day-to-day work with departments, teams and projects, that is usually the better way. Working with several Spaces has trade-offs that the Application Owners and Space Owners who set it up must accept:
>
> - **No work across Spaces.** A chat, assistant or agent only reaches the data of the active Space. A project that needs documents from two Spaces cannot use both.
> - **One Space at a time.** Users in several Spaces only reach the resources of the active Space and have to know where which data lives.
> - **Everything maintained per Space.** Members, groups, settings and data connections are set up and kept up to date in every Space separately.
> - **Costly to change later.** Merging Spaces later is not a standard operation, and data can be moved between Spaces only as an exception.
>
> Choose several Spaces only when strict separation is required, as described in [When to use several Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#when-to-use-several-spaces).

## [What’s scoped to a Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#whats-scoped-to-a-space)

The following are isolated per Space:

- **File uploads**. Files are isolated per space — the same physical file has separate identities in different spaces.
- **Collections** (built from uploaded files)
- **Assistants**
- **Prompt templates**
- **Groups**
- **Configuration**
- **Available models** (which LLMs appear in the model picker)
- **Chats**

If you upload a file in Space A, it does not exist in Space B. The same applies to every other resource above.

A user only has access to the resources of the active Space. They cannot access resources of several Spaces at the same time.

## [Confidential Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#confidential-spaces)

A Space can be marked as confidential by its Space Owner. Every chat in a confidential Space is restricted to Telekom-hosted models, and features that send data to external providers are switched off. See [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/#confidential-spaces).

## [Membership](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#membership)

- A user can be a member of one or multiple Spaces.
- A user is **active in only one Space at a time**.

## [When to use several Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#when-to-use-several-spaces)

One Space per organization is the default. Departments, teams and projects are modelled with [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) inside that Space. Several Spaces are only needed when data or administration must be strictly separated:

- Legal or compliance requirements demand strict data separation, for example between the legal entities of a group.
- Administration must be strictly separated: the Space Owners of one unit must not manage the members of another.

If users work across units, or need data from several of them, use groups instead.

## [Default Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#default-space)

Every Smartchat instance comes with a **Default space** that all users belong to. It cannot be deleted or renamed, and it is not visible in the Chat Interface.

---

# Workspace

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/

> The place in the UI where you access your collections, assistants, and prompt templates.

The **workspace** is the place in the UI where you access your data — documents, collections, assistants, and prompt templates.

Workspace contents depend on the [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/) you are currently in. Switching to another Space replaces the entire workspace with the items of that Space.

Workspace items cannot cross Space boundaries: a collection created in one Space cannot be used in another, and an assistant in one Space cannot reference collections from another. Each Space has its own isolated set of workspace items.

Who can see and edit an item is described under [Access Control](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/).

## [Workspace items](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/#workspace-items)

### [Documents](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/#documents)

Files you upload (PDFs, spreadsheets, code, plain text, etc.) that the AI can search, read, and reason over. Documents are uploaded into a Space and bundled into collections.

### [Collections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/#collections)

Named bundles of documents that the LLM can retrieve from when generating responses (RAG). Reference a collection in a chat with the **`#`** shortcut, or attach it to an assistant so it is always available.

### [Assistants](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/#assistants)

Configuration presets layered on top of a base model — pick an LLM, then bind a system prompt, knowledge collections, tools, and parameter overrides to it. Useful for repeatable tasks where the same prompt and context apply every time.

### [Prompt Templates](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/workspace/#prompt-templates)

Reusable prompts with placeholder variables (e.g. `Write an email to {{Name}}`). Invoke them in a chat with the **`/`** shortcut and fill in the variables before sending.

---

# Supported File Types

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/supported-file-types/

> The file formats Smartchat can extract and index, grouped by category.

Smartchat extracts the content of a file with a parser built for its format, then indexes it with an embedding model so it can be found during chats. Only formats with a parser can be ingested — this page lists them.

The same list applies everywhere a file enters a Space: manual upload, [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/), and [Confluence Sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/).

## [Formats](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/supported-file-types/#formats)

| Category | File types |
| - | - |
| Text documents | `pdf`, `doc`, `docx`, `rtf`, `epub` |
| Presentations | `ppt`, `pptx` |
| Spreadsheets | `xls`, `xlsx`, `csv` |
| Text and markup | `txt`, `md`, `html`, `xml`, `json` |
| Email | `msg`, `mbox` |
| Source code | `py`, `pyw`, `pyi`, `js`, `mjs`, `cjs`, `jsx`, `ts`, `tsx`, `mts`, `go`, `rs`, `java`, `c`, `h`, `cpp`, `hpp`, `cc`, `cs`, `rb`, `php`, `swift`, `kt`, `scala`, `sh`, `bash`, `sql` |
| Audio | `mp3` |

Audio files are transcribed to text before indexing.

> **Note**
>
> The list changes over time. Formats are added as parsers become available, and rarely used ones may be removed.

## [If a format is not listed](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/supported-file-types/#if-a-format-is-not-listed)

Convert the file to a supported format before uploading it — for example, export to PDF or DOCX. If ingestion fails for a file whose format *is* listed, see [Ingestion Errors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/).

## [See also](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/supported-file-types/#see-also)

- [File Size Limits](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/) — file size, page and text volume cutoffs

---

# File Size Limits

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/

> How large a file may be to reach a Smartchat space and be indexed, covering the file size limit, the PDF page limit, the limit on how much text a file may contain, why the limits exist, and how very large files are handled.

When you add a file to a space, either by uploading it or automatically through [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) or Confluence Sync, Smartchat splits the file into small chunks and indexes them so they can be found during chats. Very large files produce a huge number of chunks, which is slow to process and memory-intensive. To keep ingestion reliable for everyone, a single file can only be so large.

## [The limits](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#the-limits)

Size is limited in a few ways: how many megabytes the file has, how many pages a PDF has, and how much text it contains.

| Limit | Applies to | Maximum |
| - | - | - |
| **File size** | Files you upload in Smartchat | **100 MB** |
| **File size** | Files added through the eRAG API | **200 MB** |
| **Pages** | PDF files | **500 pages** |
| **Text volume** | Every file (including PDFs) | roughly **2,000 chunks** (very roughly **2 million tokens**, or a few thousand pages of plain text) |

A **chunk** is a slice of the document of about 1,000 tokens (a token is roughly ¾ of a word). The exact chunk size depends on your space’s configuration, so the equivalent word or page count varies.

A file needs to stay within every limit that applies to it — a PDF, for example, within the file size, page and text volume limits alike.

The limits take effect at different points: a file above the file size limit is refused when you upload it and never reaches the space, while a file that is too long is uploaded but **not ingested**, so it cannot be used in chats.

> **Note**
>
> Files up to 100 MB can be uploaded in Smartchat directly, in **Workspace → Collection**. Larger files, up to 200 MB, can only be added through the eRAG API, see [Uploading Many Files at Once](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/).

## [Why there is a hard limit](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#why-there-is-a-hard-limit)

The text volume limit is a deliberate safety cutoff. The servers that process ingestion have a finite amount of memory, and an arbitrarily large file could consume all of it and destabilise processing for other files and spaces. Because processing has to stay within that memory, a file has to be rejected at *some* size to keep the system stable, so the exact cutoff is, frankly, somewhat arbitrary. It is set well above what real documents need: the large majority of files (well over 99%) are far smaller than the limit and are never affected.

## [Large files take longer to process](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#large-files-take-longer-to-process)

A large file simply takes longer to ingest, because there is more content to split and index. That slowness comes from the size of the file itself, not from how Smartchat handles it.

To keep these long-running jobs from holding up smaller files, Smartchat processes large files (roughly above 100 pages, or around 400 chunks) on a **separate queue**. That queue is not slower or less powerful; it has the same resources as the main one. It simply keeps large files out of the way so quick files are not stuck behind them, and it allows a job the longer time it needs to finish. You do not need to do anything; large files just finish later.

Files brought in automatically by [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) always use this separate queue, so large synced files never hold up other ingestion. The size limits above are exactly the same for synced files as for uploaded ones.

## [If a file is too large](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#if-a-file-is-too-large)

- **Split it into smaller files.** For example, break a large PDF into page ranges, or a long document into per-section files. Each part is ingested separately.
- **Remove content that does not need to be searchable** (for example, large image-only appendices) before ingesting.

---

# Ingestion Errors

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/

> What the ingestion statuses of a file mean, why a file fails to ingest, and what you can do about each cause.

When you add a file to a space, either by uploading it manually or automatically through [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) or [Confluence Sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/), Smartchat extracts its text, splits it into chunks, and indexes them so they can be found during chats. Each file moves through the same lifecycle, and its collection in **Workspace → Collection** shows the current status.

Most files ingest without a hitch. When one doesn’t, the status and error message tell you why. This page explains the statuses, the common causes of failure, and what you can do about each.

## [Ingestion statuses](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#ingestion-statuses)

| Status | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **pending** | The file is queued or currently being processed. This is normal and temporary. |
| **ingested** | The file was processed successfully and is searchable in the space. |
| **ingestion\_failed** | Processing was attempted (and automatically retried) but did not succeed. The file is **not** available in the space. Check the error message for details about what went wrong. |
| **migrated** | The file exceeded the time limit on the standard processing queue and has been moved to the [large-file queue](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#large-files-take-longer-to-process) for reprocessing. This is a temporary state; the file will eventually finish as `ingested` or `ingestion_failed`. |
| **hit\_rate\_limit** | Processing is paused because the embedding service is temporarily rate-limited. You don’t have to do anything; the file will be retried in the next available time window. This is a temporary state. |

> **Note**
>
> Transient problems are retried automatically a few times before a file is marked `ingestion_failed`, so a failed status means the error persisted across retries; it is not a one-off blip.

## [Why a file fails](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#why-a-file-fails)

Almost every `ingestion_failed` file falls into one of the categories below. When a file fails, the collection shows a detailed error message next to the status. The headings below match those error messages so you can look yours up directly.

### [No nodes were generated for this document.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#no-nodes-were-generated-for-this-document)

The most common cause. Smartchat indexes **text**; if it extracts nothing from a document, there is nothing to index and ingestion fails.

This typically happens with:

- **Scanned PDFs**: pages that are photographs or scans of paper, with no underlying text layer.
- **Image-only documents**: a PDF whose pages are entirely images (diagrams, screenshots, a word cloud / “Wortwolke”, a poster).
- Files where the real content lives only in images that the extractor cannot read as text.

**What you can do:**

- Provide a **text-based version** of the document instead of a scan.
- Run **OCR** (optical character recognition) on the file first so it gains a text layer, then re-upload it.
- If only part of the document is image-only, a version with a proper text layer will ingest the readable parts.

### [Error occurred while reading the file.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#error-occurred-while-reading-the-file)

The file cannot be parsed because it is broken, truncated, or was written by a tool that does not follow the file-format specification. For PDFs this shows up as read errors deep in the parser (for example, a broken internal image stream, or a malformed page-numbering table).

**What you can do:**

- **Re-export or repair the file.** Open it in a viewer and use *Print to PDF* / *Save as PDF*, or re-export it from the original source, then upload the fresh copy. This regenerates a clean file and resolves most parser errors.
- Confirm the file opens correctly in a normal viewer; if it is visibly broken there, it needs to be regenerated at the source.

### [File extension is not supported](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#file-extension-is-not-supported)

The file’s extension is not on the list of supported formats. Smartchat processes common document and text formats; other types (executables, archives, raw media files, etc.) are rejected during ingestion.

**What you can do:** convert the content to a supported format (PDF, DOCX, TXT, or another format listed in your deployment’s documentation) and upload it again.

### [Task size exceeds the allowed limit.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#task-size-exceeds-the-allowed-limit)

The file produces more chunks than the per-file limit allows. See [File Size Limits](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/) for the exact limits.

**What you can do:** split the document into smaller files, or remove content that does not need to be searchable.

### [OpenAI rate limit exceeded.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#openai-rate-limit-exceeded)

The embedding service enforces a tokens-per-minute (TPM) limit. During ingestion the worker splits text into batches and halves the batch size on each rate-limit retry. When the batch is down to a single chunk and still exceeds the TPM budget, no further splitting is possible and the file fails permanently.

**What you can do:** ask your platform operators to either reduce the configured chunk size or increase the TPM rate limit on the API key used for embedding.

### [Task hit soft time limit even after migrating to large queue.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#task-hit-soft-time-limit-even-after-migrating-to-large-queue)

The file took too long to process and timed out on both the standard and the large-file processing queue. **Retrying will not help**; the file will still exceed the maximum allowed processing time.

**What you can do:** split the document into smaller files, or remove content that does not need to be searchable. See [File Size Limits](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/) for guidance.

### [File was not found.](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#file-was-not-found)

The file reference exists but the actual file is missing from storage. There are two cases:

- **Synced content** ([S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/), [Confluence Sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/), or other data connections): the file was removed from the source after ingestion was already queued. This is correct behavior; there is nothing to do. If you still need the file, add it back to the source.
- **Manual uploads**: this should not happen and indicates an error. Delete the file from the space and upload it again.

### [Transient or infrastructure errors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#transient-or-infrastructure-errors)

Occasionally a file fails because of a temporary condition: an API timeout, a storage hiccup, or a processing component being briefly unavailable. These are retried automatically, and most recover on their own. If a file fails and you believe the file itself is fine, re-trigger ingestion a little later. If it keeps failing, raise it with your platform operators.

The following error messages fall into this category:

- `OpenAI API error occurred.`: a temporary error from the embedding service.
- `Cannot connect to Postgres Database.`: the database was briefly unreachable.
- `Cannot connect to S3 file system.`: object storage was briefly unreachable.
- `Pipeline could not be built.`: the processing pipeline failed to initialize; this is typically an infrastructure issue.

## [Files stuck as “pending”](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#files-stuck-as-pending)

`pending` is a normal, temporary state, but a file that stays pending for a long time with no progress is worth a look. This is **not** the same as a failure: the file has not errored, it simply has not finished (or started) processing.

Common reasons:

- **Large files take longer.** Big documents are processed on a [separate queue](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/#large-files-take-longer-to-process) and finish later by design. A large file sitting in `pending` for a while is expected. You may see the status change to `migrated` while the file moves to the large-file queue; it will resolve to `ingested` or `ingestion_failed` once processing completes.
- **Queue backlog.** During a large bulk import, files wait their turn behind everything already queued.
- **The job was never picked up.** More rarely, a file is never scheduled for processing, for example because of an ingestion-service disruption. In this case the file shows no processing activity at all.

**What you can do:** give large files and big batches time to work through the queue. In very busy systems, especially in the large-file queue, this can take hours up to days. Retrying earlier just increases the queue pressure and does not help.

Only retry a file if the queue is empty (i.e. new files get processed instantly) but the file you want is still stuck in `pending`. This indicates the task was permanently lost and the pending state is stuck. If it still does not move after retrying, raise it with your Application Owner or platform operators.

## [Getting more detail](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/#getting-more-detail)

For deeper investigation, the ingestion service also records the full error (including the file, the internal task, and the underlying exception) in its logs. If you need more context than the error message provides, ask your platform operators to check the ingestion worker logs for that file.

---

# Agent Mode

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/

> What Agent Mode is, how to turn it on, and how agents use connectors to work with your organisation's tools.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode and MCP connectors are currently in preview only. If you would like to test these features, please contact your T-Systems representative.

In **Agent Mode**, Smartchat answers with an agent instead of a single model call. An agent plans its own steps: it can run code in a sandbox, call tools, and work with your organisation’s own systems through [connectors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/). It decides by itself when a tool or connector helps with your request.

## [Turning on Agent Mode](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/#turning-on-agent-mode)

Switch on the **Agent Mode** toggle in the message box before you send the first message of a chat. Off means a regular chat. A new chat starts in the mode you last picked in that Space. If you have not picked one there, it follows the Space’s default, which Space Owners and Application Owners set in the [Agent Mode Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/).

The mode is fixed per chat:

- **It cannot be changed once the chat has started.** Start a new chat to switch between Agent Mode and a regular chat.
- **It cannot be changed while a file uploaded for the agent is attached.** Remove the file first.

## [Choosing an agent](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/#choosing-an-agent)

Where several agents are available, pick one with **Switch agent**. Each agent can come with its own instructions, example prompts and connectors. To build your own agents, see [Custom Agents](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/custom-agents/).

## [Attaching files](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/#attaching-files)

When the selected agent has a sandbox, you can attach files of any type to the chat, up to 100 MB per file and 20 files per message. The files go to the agent directly and are not added to a collection. If the agent has no sandbox, it cannot read uploaded files, and Smartchat asks you to select an agent with a sandbox.

## [Web access](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/#web-access)

> **Off by default since v3.15.1**
>
> Agents can use the web only when an Application Owner allows it for the instance in Administration and the Space Owner then allows it for their Space. Until both have, the agent editor shows the agent’s web capabilities as disabled. Confidential Spaces and chats never get web access.

Application Owners and Space Owners find these switches in the [Agent Mode Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/).

## [Working with an agent](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/#working-with-an-agent)

- **Approvals**: before some actions, the agent asks for your approval. Approve or decline in the chat to let it continue.
- **Turn limit**: an agent stops after a fixed number of steps. Your request is still valid: ask the agent to continue from where it stopped.
- **Connectors**: if the agent needs a connector you have not connected yet, it asks you to connect it first. See [Using Connectors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/).
- **Stop Agent** ends a run at any time.

Agents always work with your own permissions. They can never show you anything your account could not already see.

---

# Artifacts

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/artifacts/

> Find, open, download, continue editing and delete the files that agents produce.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode and its artifacts are currently in preview only. If you would like to test these features, please contact your T-Systems representative.

**Artifacts** are the files an agent produces in [Agent Mode](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/), such as spreadsheets, presentations or documents. They are kept per Space, so you find them again after the chat.

## [In the chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/artifacts/#in-the-chat)

Every file an agent created in this chat.

- Each file the agent delivers appears as a card under its answer, with **Open** and **Download**. A card marks a file that was deleted since.
- **Artifacts** in the chat header, with the number of files, opens a panel with all of the chat’s artifacts, including those from earlier sessions.

## [The Artifacts page](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/artifacts/#the-artifacts-page)

**Artifacts** in the sidebar, below the Workspace, lists all artifacts of the active Space. Search by name, sort by any column, and click an artifact to open its page: its type and details, **Download**, and a link back to the chat that produced it.

Artifacts without a chat stay here too.

## [Continuing to edit an artifact](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/artifacts/#continuing-to-edit-an-artifact)

1. Choose **Continue editing** in an artifact’s row menu, or click the **Continue editing** button on the artifact’s page.

   Continue editing opens the chat the artifact came from.

2. Smartchat opens the chat the artifact came from, or a new chat if it has none. The artifact is shown above the message box.

3. Describe your changes and send the message. An agent with a sandbox updates the file instead of making a second one.

## [Deleting artifacts](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/artifacts/#deleting-artifacts)

- **Delete** in an artifact’s row menu or on its page deletes it after a confirmation.
- When you delete a chat that has artifacts, the confirmation lists them and offers **Also delete its artifacts**. It is unchecked, so the artifacts stay on the Artifacts page unless you tick it.

The option is unticked: without it, the artifacts stay.

---

# Using Connectors

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/

> Connect an agent to tools like Telecontext with your own account, use them in a chat, and disconnect again.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode and MCP connectors are currently in preview only. If you would like to test these features, please contact your T-Systems representative.

A **connector** links Smartchat to one of your organisation’s systems through the [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/). Once you have connected it, an agent can read data from that system and use its functions during a chat.

Connectors are registered by the operators of Smartchat, and an Application Owner or Space Owner decides who in the Space may use them. You cannot add your own; you only decide which of the available ones to connect with your account.

## [Connecting a connector](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/#connecting-a-connector)

1. Open a chat and switch on **Agent Mode**. Connectors are only available to agents.

2. Click **Connect a tool** below the message box. The **Connectors** dialog lists every connector made available in your Space.

   *\[Image: Connectors dialog with the available connectors]*

3. Click **Connect** on the connector you want. Smartchat shows what it will be able to do once you approve:

   - read the data you already have access to,
   - use the connector’s tools on your behalf during a chat,
   - act only while you are signed in. Access ends when you disconnect.

   *\[Image: Consent dialog before connecting]*

4. Click **Authorize with** followed by the connector’s name. A new window opens with the sign-in page of that system, for example your Microsoft login.

5. Sign in and approve the permissions the system asks for.

   *\[Image: Sign-in and approval page of the connected system]*

6. Back in Smartchat, the dialog confirms that the connector is ready to use, and the connector shows as **Connected**.

> **Tip**
>
> If your browser blocks the sign-in window, use the **Open the sign-in page** link in the dialog.

You sign in on the system’s own page. Smartchat never sees your password.

## [Using a connector in a chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/#using-a-connector-in-a-chat)

A connected connector is not active in every chat automatically. In the **Connectors** dialog, switch on **Use in this chat** for each connector the agent should use. Active connectors are listed under **Active in this chat** below the message box.

*\[Image: Connected connector with the Use in this chat switch]*

Then ask your question as usual. The agent decides when to call the connector.

*\[Image: Agent answering with data from a connected system]*

Because you connected with your own account, the agent only sees what you can see in that system. Two colleagues using the same connector each work with their own data and permissions.

## [Disconnecting](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/#disconnecting)

Open the **Connectors** dialog and click **Disconnect** on the connector. For a few seconds you can still **Undo**. After that, Smartchat’s access ends; to use the connector again, connect it again.

You may also be asked to connect again when a connector’s registration is renewed, your access is revoked and granted back, or your connector’s access token has expired or been revoked.

---

# Managing Connectors

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/

> How MCP servers are registered as connectors, and how Application Owners and Space Owners decide who in a Space may use them.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode and MCP connectors are currently in preview only. If you would like to test these features, please contact your T-Systems representative.

Connectors bring MCP servers into Smartchat. Making one available takes two steps:

1. The MCP server is **registered** for the whole instance. This is done by the operators of Smartchat. To add a server, contact your T-Systems representative with the server’s URL.
2. In each Space, an Application Owner or Space Owner decides **who may use** the connector.

Users can never add MCP servers themselves. Every connector is approved by an administrator, so your organisation decides which systems Smartchat talks to.

## [Registering an MCP server](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/#registering-an-mcp-server)

A connector needs a **Name** and the server’s **URL**, plus an optional **Description** that users see. No API key or password is entered.

*\[Image: Add connector dialog with name and URL]*

When you click **Provision connector**, Smartchat discovers the server’s sign-in endpoints and registers itself with the server as an OAuth client (dynamic client registration). The client secret is stored in Smartchat’s secret store. From then on, each user signs in to the server with their own account when they [connect](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/connectors/).

The server therefore has to support OAuth 2.1 with the authorization code flow, PKCE and dynamic client registration.

*\[Image: Provisioned connector with its endpoints, client ID and scopes]*

A new connector is usable by everyone in every Space until access is restricted per Space.

### [Renewing the registration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/#renewing-the-registration)

**Sync** registers Smartchat with the server again and creates a new client. All users who had connected are disconnected and have to connect again the next time they use the connector.

*\[Image: Sync connector dialog warning that everyone who had connected loses access]*

## [Choosing who can use a connector](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/managing-connectors/#choosing-who-can-use-a-connector)

Application Owners and Space Owners control access per Space in **Workspace → Connectors**. The page lists every registered connector with three options:

| Option | Who can use the connector in this Space |
| - | - |
| **Public** | Every member of the Space. This is the default. |
| **Admin** | Application Owners only. |
| **Group** | Members of the [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) you select. |

*\[Image: Workspace Connectors tab with Public, Admin and Group options]*

Space Owners can do this for the Spaces they own. Application Owners can do it for every Space they are a member of. The setting applies to the Space shown in the Space selector.

---

# Custom Agents

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/custom-agents/

> Who can build and share custom agents in a Space, and how Space Owners grant the permission.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode and MCP connectors are currently in preview only. If you would like to test these features, please contact your T-Systems representative.

Besides the agents that come with Smartchat, you can build your own agents in **Workspace → Agents → New agent**, with their own instructions, example prompts and connectors. Building custom agents is only available where the operators of Smartchat have enabled it for you.

*\[Image: Agents in Workspace]*

*\[Image: New agent access]*

## [Permissions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/custom-agents/#permissions)

Two permissions control custom agents:

| Permission | Where to find it | Allows |
| - | - | - |
| **Agent Management** | **Workspace Permissions** | Building, editing and deleting custom agents. Without it, the **Agents** tab does not appear in the Workspace. |
| **Agents Public Sharing** | **Sharing Permissions** | Making an agent available to everyone in the Space. Sharing an agent with specific groups does not need this permission. |

Both permissions are off in a new Space. Like every [permission](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/), they apply only in their Space, and a custom agent is only available in the Space it was built in.

Space Owners always have both permissions in their own Space, without belonging to a group. Application Owners have them in every Space where they also hold a Space role.

## [Granting the permission](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/custom-agents/#granting-the-permission)

Space Owners grant the permissions through [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) in their Space:

1. Click your profile image and choose **Administration**.
2. Go to **Space Owner → Groups** and check that the right Space is selected.
3. Click on a group, or click **Default permissions** to grant the permission to every member of the Space. Only Application Owners see **Default permissions**.
4. Open the **Permissions** tab.
5. Under **Workspace Permissions**, enable **Agent Management**. To allow sharing agents with the whole Space, also enable **Agents Public Sharing** under **Sharing Permissions**.
6. If you edited a group, add the users who should build agents to it on the **Users** tab.

*\[Image: Agent permissions]*

The two switches only appear when building custom agents is available to you. Who can use or edit an agent once it is built is decided when it is [shared](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/access-control/).

---

# Glossary

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/glossary/

> Glossary of key terms used in Smartchat.

| Term | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Application Owner** | Global responsibility for the entire Smartchat application; can manage all spaces and users. |
| **API Key** | A unique access key that allows external systems to securely access Smartchat functionality. |
| **Workspace** | An area for creating, editing, or deleting custom resources (assistants, knowledge collections, prompt templates). |
| **Workspace Resources** | Three categories: assistants, custom knowledge, and custom prompt templates, each individually created/customized. |
| **Auto-Sync** | Automated synchronization: automatic data upload from a linked data source. |
| **Cloud Environment** | An externally operated computing system that provides data and programs over the internet, rather than storing them locally. |
| **Confidential** | Marks data that may only be processed by Telekom-hosted models and must not be sent to external providers. Set per collection or per Space; a chat that uses such data becomes a confidential chat. See [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/). |
| **Advanced Parameters** | Additional settings for fine-tuning a function or model. |
| **Ingestion Configuration** | The process of integrating data from a data source. Various configurations can be set for ingestion (speed vs. accuracy). |
| **LLM** | Large Language Model: an AI model for processing and generating text. |
| **Multimodal Model** | An AI model that can process different data types (e.g. text and images). |
| **Prompt** | User input (question or instruction to an AI). |
| **Privacy mode** | Earlier name of confidentiality in the release notes (“Lightweight Privacy Mode”). See [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/). |
| **PSA DSK3-compliant** | Approved in the Privacy & Security Assessment (PSA) for data protection class 3 (DSK3). |
| **RAG** | Retrieval Augmented Generation: context-based document search with language model support. |
| **Space** | Smartchat’s tenant boundary. Every resource (files, collections, assistants, chats, …) belongs to exactly one Space and is isolated from all other Spaces. See [Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/). |
| **Assistants** | Configurations built on top of an existing AI model, combining a system prompt and knowledge, tailored to specific tasks and shared with others in the Space. |
| **Custom Prompt Templates** | Templates for standardizing repetitive queries. |
| **Custom Knowledge** | Can be used as context in individual chats and with assistants. |
| **Single Sign-On (SSO)** | A procedure where the user logs in once and can then access multiple applications without re-authenticating. |
| **System Prompt** | A predefined technical background instruction that is always included by a model. |
| **Tag** | A short keyword marker for categorizing chat histories. |

---

# Administration

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/

> How Application Owners and Space Owners manage Spaces, users, settings and data connections directly in Smartchat.

Smartchat is administered directly in the app. The **Administration** area covers everything Application Owners and Space Owners need: Spaces and their owners, users and their roles, the settings of each Space (confidentiality, API key, models), and the data connections that feed content into a Space. Regular users do not see it.

> **The legacy admin panel is being retired**
>
> Everything the separate admin panel at `admin-panel.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net` could do is now part of **Administration** in Smartchat. The legacy admin panel will be switched off at the end of October 2026.

## [Opening Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/#opening-administration)

Click your profile image at the bottom left and choose **Administration**. The entry is only shown to Application Owners and Space Owners.

*\[Image: User menu with the Administration entry]*

Administration opens with a navigation of its own on the left. It is divided into one section per role, and you only see the sections your role gives you:

| Section | For | What you do there |
| - | - | - |
| **Application Owner** | Application Owners | Manage all [Spaces and users](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/) of the instance, and settings that apply to the whole instance (**Interface**, **Code Execution**). |
| **Space Owner** | Space Owners | Manage the [members](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/) and groups of a Space, its [settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/), and its [Confluence](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/) and [S3](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) sources. |

**Search settings** at the top finds any page of Administration by name. **Back to Chat** returns to your chats.

*\[Image: Administration with the Application Owner and Space Owner sections]*

## [Choosing the Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/#choosing-the-space)

Everything under **Space Owner** acts on one Space at a time. Pick it in the **Selected Space** picker at the top of the section. To administer another Space you own, switch it there.

*\[Image: Selected Space picker in the Space Owner section]*

The **Space Owner** section shows these pages:

| Group | Pages |
| - | - |
| **Manage** | **Space Members**, **Feedback**, **Groups** |
| **Settings** | **Models**, **Space**, **Data Connections**, **S3 AutoSync**, **Web Search** |

> **Note**
>
> **Data Connections** and **S3 AutoSync** are only shown when the integration is enabled for your Smartchat environment. **Web Search** appears when per-Space web search configuration is enabled.

## [Who has access](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/#who-has-access)

- **Application Owner**: sees the **Application Owner** section and can open the Space settings of the Spaces they belong to. **Space Members** is only shown for Spaces they also own: adding and removing members is reserved for Space Owners.
- **Space Owner**: sees the **Space Owner** section for every Space they own. Other Spaces cannot be administered.

For the full capability list see [Roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/).

---

# Managing Spaces and Users

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/

> How Application Owners create and configure Spaces and manage users and their Space roles across the whole instance.

The **Application Owner** section of [Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/) is where Application Owners manage the whole Smartchat instance: every Space, every user, and the settings that apply to everyone. Open it with **Administration → Application Owner**.

## [Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#spaces)

**Spaces** lists every Space of the instance with its number of members, its Space Owners and its creation date. A column shows which Spaces hold confidential data, and you can switch confidentiality on or off for a Space directly in that column.

Click a Space to open its configuration:

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Name** | The Space’s name as members see it in the Space selector. |
| **Confidential Data** | Treats all data in the Space as confidential. See [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/). |
| **IdP auto-assignment attribute** | Links the Space to an attribute from your identity provider, for example an Active Directory group. Everyone who signs in with that attribute is added to the Space automatically. See [IdP attribute to Space membership](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-space-membership). |
| **Space API Key** | The key Smartchat uses to reach model serving for this Space. Once saved, it is only shown masked. |
| **Max. number of members** | How many members the Space may have. **0** means unlimited. |
| **Members** | The members and their roles. Add members by email, one at a time or several at once, switch a member between **User** and **Space Owner**, or remove them. |

*\[Image: Space configuration with confidentiality, IdP attribute, API key and members]*

### [Creating a Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#creating-a-space)

Click **New space** above the list to create a Space. The dialog configures it completely in one step; see [Setting Up a New Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/setting-up-a-new-space/).

## [Users](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#users)

**Users** lists everyone registered on the instance, including people who have been added but have **never signed in**, with their creation date and the Spaces they belong to.

A badge marks accounts that are not your organisation’s users: **Service account** for SmartChat’s own technical accounts, **Internal** for T-Systems staff and **Test account** for test accounts. Service accounts cannot be deleted or removed from a Space. The badges also appear in a Space’s member list.

Click a user to open **Edit user**. It shows every Space the user belongs to and every role they hold in it, including the Default Space:

- Add the user to another Space, or take a Space away.
- Switch a role between **User** and **Space Owner**.
- Switch **Application Owner** on or off for the user.

**Add users** above the list opens the same dialog empty, so you can give Spaces and roles to people who are not listed yet. Addresses without an account are marked **Will be created**.

Click **Save** to apply the changes. The dialog shows what will happen before you save: which Spaces **will be added**, which **will be taken away**, and whose role changes.

*\[Image: Edit user dialog with the user’s Spaces and roles]*

### [One user or several](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#one-user-or-several)

The switch next to **Email** sets how many people the dialog changes:

- **One user**: a single email address.
- **Several users at once**: one email address per row. The clipboard button next to the rows takes a whole list of addresses at once. The Spaces, roles and **Application Owner** setting below apply to every listed user. The dialog tells you when a list is longer than your instance allows in one go.

### [Add or replace](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#add-or-replace)

The switch next to **Cancel** sets what happens to the Spaces the users already have:

- **Add** (plus icon): the users keep the Spaces they have and get the ones listed in the dialog as well. Adding never takes anything away, so it does not revoke **Application Owner** either.
- **Replace** (arrows icon): the users end up with exactly the Spaces listed in the dialog and lose every other one. **Application Owner** is revoked when its switch is off.

**Edit user** starts in **Replace**, because the dialog already lists all of the user’s Spaces. **Add users** starts in **Add**. Replacing for several users at once shows a warning, because each of them loses every Space that is not in the list.

**You cannot revoke your own Application Owner role.** Ask another Application Owner.

Spaces assigned by your identity provider stay assigned, whatever you change here.

### [People who have never signed in](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#people-who-have-never-signed-in)

On instances with [account creation only through your identity provider](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#account-creation-only-through-your-identity-provider) enabled, you cannot add someone to Smartchat for the first time and to a Space in one step: their account is only created when they first sign in. Wait until they have signed in once through single sign-on, then add them. The two dialogs for adding people handle such a person differently:

- **Add users** (here, under **Users**) does not let you save them: **Save** stays disabled, and the dialog explains why next to their email with **Not signed in yet, so they cannot be added.** When you add several users at once, remove that address to save the others.
- **Add new member** (in a Space’s members, see [Managing Space Members](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/)) only finds out when you click **Add**. A single member is then rejected with a message that they have not signed in yet. When you add several members at once, the whole list is rejected and every member of it is shown as not added.

## [Instance settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#instance-settings)

**Interface** and **Code Execution** hold settings that apply to the whole instance, for example banners and the prompt suggestions shown on the start screen. Changes affect all users.

Agent Mode has its own settings, see [Agent Mode Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/).

---

# Setting Up a New Space

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/setting-up-a-new-space/

> How an Application Owner creates a new Space and configures it in one step.

Application Owners create Spaces in [Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/). The Space is fully configured when it is created: API key, models, confidentiality and its first Space Owners are all set in the same dialog.

> **Is a new Space really needed?**
>
> Do not create a Space per department, team or project: use [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) and collections within the existing Space instead. Splitting into several Spaces is costly to change later, and users cannot work with data from several Spaces at once. Create a new Space only when strict separation is required, as described in [When to use several Spaces](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/spaces/#when-to-use-several-spaces).

## [Creating the Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/setting-up-a-new-space/#creating-the-space)

Open **Administration → Application Owner → Spaces** and click **New space**:

1. Enter a **Name**. It must be unique on the instance.
2. Paste the **Space API Key** obtained from the [API Key Portal](https://apikey.llmhub.t-systems.net/) and press **Enter**. The model lists load once a key is entered.
3. Pick the **Embedding Model** and the **Default Model**. The embedding model cannot be changed after the Space is created.
4. Optionally enter an **IdP auto-assignment attribute** and switch on **Confidential Data**.
5. Add at least one email under **Space Owners**.
6. Click **Create**.

**Copy settings from** at the top of the dialog fills in everything except the name and the owners from an existing Space: API key, embedding model, default model, confidentiality and IdP attribute.

*\[Image: New space dialog with the Copy settings from menu]*

The new owners see the Space in their Space selector after their next login. From then on they [manage its members](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/) and can connect content sources such as [Confluence](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/) or an [S3 bucket](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/).

> **Caution**
>
> Without a usable Space API key, or without an embedding model and a default language model, nobody can work in the Space: signing in to it or switching to it fails with an error that asks a Space Owner to check the configuration.

> **Tip**
>
> The default model does not have to be a plain language model. You can also set it to an [assistant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants), so every new chat in the Space starts with its system prompt and knowledge already applied.

---

# Space Settings

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/

> Confidentiality, Space API key, upload limit and models: the settings a Space Owner controls in Administration.

The **Settings** pages of the **Space Owner** section in [Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/) hold the configuration of a Space. This page covers the **Space**, **Models** and **Web Search** pages; data sources have their own guides ([Confluence Sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/), [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/)).

Open **Administration → Space Owner** and pick the Space you want to configure in **Selected Space**.

## [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#space)

*\[Image: Space page with the Confidential Data switch and the Space API Key field]*

### [Confidential Data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#confidential-data)

The **Confidential Data** switch marks every chat in this Space as confidential, restricting it to models that may process confidential data. Turning it on:

- locks all chats in the Space to Telekom-hosted models, externally hosted models are refused,
- disables web search and tools in those chats,
- applies to every collection of the Space, regardless of the collection’s own confidentiality flag.

If web search is configured for the Space, Smartchat first asks you to confirm (**Mark this space as confidential?**) and then switches web search off for the Space. Its settings are kept and apply again once the Space is no longer confidential.

The change is saved immediately (toast **Space configuration saved**) and members see the confidential badge in the chat composer without reloading. How confidentiality propagates to collections and chats is explained in [Confidentiality](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/confidentiality/).

### [Space API Key](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#space-api-key)

Smartchat needs a key from the [API Key Portal](https://apikey.llmhub.t-systems.net/) to reach model serving on behalf of the Space.

1. Paste the key into **Space API Key** and press **Enter** (or click outside the field). The toast **Space API key saved** confirms the update.
2. The hint below the field tells you the state: **A key is configured. Enter a new one to replace it.** or **No key is configured. This space cannot reach model serving without one.**

> **The key is write-only**
>
> Since v3.15.1, nobody can read a saved key: Space Owners and Application Owners see only whether a key is configured, and `GET /space/api-key` no longer returns it either. Keep the key in your team’s secret store. To rotate it, paste the new key over the placeholder.

### [Max Upload Size](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#max-upload-size)

Where upload control is enabled for your environment, **Max Upload Size** limits the size of a single file upload in MB. Leave it empty for no limit. The value is saved when you leave the field.

### [Feedback](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#feedback)

Where feedback is available for your environment, the **Feedback** switch lets the members of this Space [rate responses](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/) and share them with you. Turning it off hides the rating buttons; feedback given before is kept and stays on the [Feedback](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/feedback/) page.

## [Models](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#models)

Where Agent Mode is available, its settings for this Space (default mode for new chats, web access for agents) are described in [Agent Mode Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/#for-a-space).

*\[Image: Models page with the default model selector and the embedding model card]*

- **Enable and disable models**: the list shows all models available to the Space. Use the toggle in each row to control which ones your members can pick. **Search Models** filters the list.
- **Default model**: the model preselected for new chats in this Space. Pick a model or an [assistant](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/workspaces/#creating-and-using-assistants). If the chosen model is later withdrawn, the selector shows **The selected default model is no longer available.** and the eRAG default is used until you pick a new one.
- **Embedding Model**: shown for information only. It was set when the Space was configured and cannot be changed afterwards, because all existing embeddings depend on it.
- **Import Presets / Export Presets**: exchange model presets between Spaces as JSON.

## [Web Search](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#web-search)

The **Web Search** page has a switch for each type of web search:

- **Web Search**: searches through an external search provider. It has to be set up for your Smartchat environment first, with a search provider key that is licensed separately.
- **Enable Native Web Search**: lets Claude and Gemini models search through their own provider. It needs no setup.

A switch only appears once its type of web search is available in your environment, and it is then on in every Space. Switch it off and the Space’s users no longer get that type of web search; switch it back on to return it. In a Space marked **Confidential Data**, web search stays off whatever the switches say.

Where per-Space web search configuration is enabled, you also choose the search engine and enter its credentials for this Space only. A banner reminds you that the changes apply only to this Space.

In My Space, the page also has **Allow Web Search with Files/Collections in My Space**. While it is off, web search in My Space is not available as soon as files or collections are attached to a chat, or the selected assistant has a collection. Other Spaces don’t have this switch.

---

# Agent Mode Settings

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/

> Set the mode new chats start in and whether agents may use the web, for the whole instance and per Space.

> **Preview**
>
> Agent Mode is currently in preview only. These settings appear where it is available. If you would like to test it, please contact your T-Systems representative.

Two settings decide how [Agent Mode](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/agents/) behaves: the mode new chats start in, and whether agents may use the web. Application Owners set both for the whole instance; Space Owners can then adjust them for their Space.

## [For the whole instance](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/#for-the-whole-instance)

Application Owners find them under **Interface → Agent Mode**:

- **Default mode for new chats**: whether a new chat starts as a regular chat or in **Agent Mode**. It applies to users who have not picked a mode themselves, in Spaces without a default of their own. Existing chats keep their mode.
- **Allow agents to use the web**: off by default. While it is off, no agent can use the web, including agents that have **Use the web** selected. Switching it on asks for confirmation and lets each Space Owner decide for their Space. For My Space, the Application Owner decides.

The default mode only applies where neither the user nor the Space has chosen one.

> **Web access lets data leave SmartChat**
>
> Agents with web access can open any web page: data from chats and files can leave SmartChat in the addresses an agent opens, and a page can contain instructions that steer the agent. Confidential Spaces, chats and data never get web access.

## [For a Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/agent-mode/#for-a-space)

Space Owners find them in the [Space Settings](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/):
