- **Default mode for new chats**, on the **Models** page: the mode a new chat in this Space starts in, for members who have not picked one in this Space themselves. **Use the application default** follows the instance setting above.
- **Allow agents in this space to use the web**, on the **Space** page: lets the agents of this Space use **Use the web** when they have it selected. It is off by default, asks for confirmation, and can only be switched on once an Application Owner allows web access for the instance.

While the Application Owner blocks web access, the Space's switch cannot be turned on.

---

# Managing Space Members

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/

> Add and remove members of your Space and promote them to Space Owner, directly in Smartchat.

Space Owners manage who belongs to their Space from **Administration → Space Owner → Space Members**. The page is only shown to Space Owners and acts on the Space chosen in **Selected Space**.

*\[Image: Space Members page with the role switches and the Add User button]*

The list shows every member of the Space with four columns:

| Column | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Role** | **User** or **Space Owner**. Click the other half of the switch to change the role (see below). |
| **Email** | The member’s login. Click it to open the member’s details. |
| **Last Active** | When the member last used Smartchat. Members who have not logged in yet show no date. |
| **Created at** | When the account was created. |

## [Adding a member](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#adding-a-member)

1. Click **Add User** above the list.
2. Enter the person’s **Email** in the **Add new member** dialog and click **Add**.

*\[Image: Add new member dialog]*

What happens next depends on the email address:

- **The person already has a Smartchat account**: they are added to the Space with the **User** role and see it in their Space selector on their next page load.
- **The email is unknown**: an account is created for them. They receive an invitation email from the identity provider, and they already appear in the list with the **User** role before their first login. On instances with [account creation only through your identity provider](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#account-creation-only-through-your-identity-provider) enabled, they have to sign in once before you can add them.

New members can chat right away and use the items shared with them, such as the **{Space} - General** collection. To let them administer the Space, promote them to Space Owner.

> **Seats**
>
> If your contract limits the number of seats in a Space, adding a member beyond that limit fails with a license error. Contact support to raise the limit.

## [Adding several members at once](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#adding-several-members-at-once)

To add a whole team, switch the **Add new member** dialog to **Several members at once** (the icon next to the title) and paste the email addresses into the text box. One address per line, separated by commas or semicolons, copied recipients from Outlook (`"Doe, Jane" <jane.doe@example.com>`) and a copied column from Excel all work; duplicates are dropped automatically.

Below the box you see how many addresses were recognised. Entries that are not email addresses are listed in red and must be fixed or removed before **Add** becomes available. Then click **Add N members**.

Each address is handled like a single add: existing accounts join the Space, unknown addresses get an account and an invitation email. When the request finishes, the dialog reports how many members were added and lists any address that could not be added with the reason. **Copy failed email addresses** puts those on the clipboard so you can fix them and try again; already added members are skipped on a retry.

> **Limit**
>
> Up to 100 members can be added in one go. For larger groups, an identity provider integration (for example Entra ID) is the better fit. Contact T-Systems.

## [Changing a member’s role](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#changing-a-members-role)

A Space has two roles: **User** and **Space Owner**. Owners get everything described in [Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/); see [Roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/) for the complete matrix.

Either use the **Role** switch in the list, or open the member (click the email) and use the **Role** switch of the **Edit member** dialog.

*\[Image: Edit member dialog with the Role switch]*

The new role is applied immediately, there is no separate save step. If the update fails, the switch flips back and a toast explains why.

Two rules apply:

- **You cannot change your own role.** The switch in your own row is greyed out. Ask another owner to promote or demote you.
- **A Space keeps at least one owner.** The last remaining owner cannot be demoted or removed while the Space has other members.

## [Removing a member](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#removing-a-member)

1. Hover the member’s row and click the bin icon (**Remove user**), or open the member and click **Delete** in the **Edit member** dialog.
2. Confirm with **Remove**.

*\[Image: Remove user confirmation]*

The person loses access to the Space immediately: they are removed from the Space itself and from all of its groups, including custom groups. Their Smartchat account and their other Spaces are not affected. You cannot remove yourself.

## [Restrictions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/managing-space-members/#restrictions)

- **Space owner group**: the **SpaceOwners {Space}** group mirrors the roles above and cannot be edited, see [Groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/#groups-every-space-has). Space Owners have every [permission](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/permissions/#space-owners) of their Space.
- **Application Owners** who are not owners of a Space cannot add or remove its members here. They manage Space memberships per user under [**Application Owner → Users**](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#users).

> **Who can delete accounts**
>
> Since v3.15.1, a Space Owner can delete the account of a user who is no longer a member of any Space. Only Application Owners can delete the account of a user with an application-level role, such as Application Owner, and on instances that manage accounts through the identity provider, only Application Owners can delete accounts at all.

> **Identity fields are locked**
>
> The **Email** and **Username** of an existing member cannot be edited in Smartchat. Name and email changes come from your identity provider.

---

# Confluence Sync

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/

> How to connect a Confluence Data Center space to your Smartchat Space for automatic synchronization.

This guide explains how to set up a connection between your Smartchat Space and a Confluence Data Center instance. Once connected, Smartchat syncs the Confluence pages every night so they become searchable and available as context for your conversations.

> **Note**
>
> This feature is designed to support **Confluence Data Center 9.2.x**. Other versions may work but are not officially tested. Confluence Cloud is not supported at this time.
>
> See the [Atlassian Confluence Data Center 9.2 documentation](https://confluence.atlassian.com/conf92/confluence-data-center-documentation-1477575463.html) for details about this version.

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#prerequisites)

- You need the **Space Owner** role in the Smartchat Space. See [Roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/) for details.
- A **service account token** or **personal access token** (PAT) from the Confluence server you want to sync. Ask your Confluence administrator if you are unsure how to obtain one.
- Data connections must be enabled for your Smartchat environment. If the **Data Connections** page is missing, ask your Application Owner.

> **Understand what gets synced**
>
> The sync process has access to **all pages visible to the user account** whose credentials you provide. It cannot sync pages the user cannot see, but it **will** sync everything the user **can** see, including pages that may be considered private or sensitive.
>
> Before proceeding, make sure you are authorized to share all of that content with everyone who has access to the Smartchat Space.

## [Step 1 — Open Data Connections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#step-1--open-data-connections)

Click your profile image, choose **Administration**, and pick the Space you want to configure in **Selected Space** under **Space Owner**. Then open **Data Connections**. You will see a table listing all existing connections of this Space.

*\[Image: Data Connections page with one connection]*

## [Step 2 — Create a new connection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#step-2--create-a-new-connection)

Click **Add data connection**. The form has three sections:

*\[Image: Add data connection form]*

**Source**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | Select **Confluence**. |
| **Name** | A name for your connection: 3 to 64 letters, digits, `-` or `_`, no spaces. The name identifies the connection and cannot be changed later. |
| **URL** | The base URL of your Confluence instance, e.g. `https://example.com/confluence/` |
| **Space key** | The Confluence **space key** to sync. This is the short prefix that appears in Confluence URLs. For example, if your pages have URLs like `https://example.com/confluence/spaces/DOCS/pages/...`, the space key is `DOCS`. |

**Credentials**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Authentication** | **BASIC AUTH** for a username plus token or password, **BEARER TOKEN** for a token sent on its own. |
| **Username** | The username of the service account or personal account (Basic Auth only). |
| **Password or token** | The corresponding access token or password. |

**Synchronization**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Target collection** | Where the synced pages land. **General collection** is the Space’s default collection, visible to every member; pick another collection of the Space to sync into it instead. |
| **Active** | Leave on. Inactive connections keep their settings but are skipped by the nightly sync. |

> **Telekom Wiki (wiki.telekom.de)**
>
> If you are connecting to the internal **Telekom Wiki**, use these values:
>
> - **URL**: `https://wiki.telekom.de/` (nothing more: no `/wiki`, no path)
> - **Authentication**: **BASIC AUTH**
> - **Username**: your Telekom Wiki username. This is **case-sensitive**; for Telekom Wiki use your email address in **lowercase**
> - **Password or token**: an **API token** generated at [wiki.telekom.de → API tokens](https://wiki.telekom.de/plugins/servlet/no.kantega.kerberosauth.kerberosauth-plugin/user/api-tokens)

> **Do not use your real password**
>
> Even with **BASIC AUTH**, put the generated **API token** into the **Password or token** field, not your real account password. Basic Auth here means “send username and token as HTTP Basic credentials”, not “send your login password”.

## [Step 3 — Test and save](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#step-3--test-and-save)

Click **Test connection** at the bottom of the form. The result badge next to the button tells you whether Smartchat could reach the Confluence space with these credentials (see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#troubleshooting) for the possible results).

Click **Save**. On success the toast **Connection saved and nightly sync scheduled.** appears and the connection is listed in the table. If the test fails, the connection is still saved but its sync stays paused until you fix the settings and save again.

## [Step 4 — Verify the connection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#step-4--verify-the-connection)

*\[Image: Connection row with status and actions]*

| Column | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Status** | **Active** (green) or **Inactive**. |
| **Documents** | Number of pages synced so far. |
| **Next sync** | When the next nightly run is due, or **Paused**. |
| **Last sync** | Date of the last successful run. |

Click the connection’s **Name** to copy it to the clipboard.

## [Attachments](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#attachments)

Besides the pages, Smartchat also syncs the attachments of the synced pages into the same **Target collection**. By default, attachments of these types are synced, up to 50 MB each: PDF, Word (`doc`, `docx`), PowerPoint (`ppt`, `pptx`), Excel (`xls`, `xlsx`), `csv`, `txt`, `md`, `html`, `xml`, `json`, `rtf`, `epub`, `msg`, `mbox` and `mp3`. When an attachment or its page is deleted in Confluence, it is removed from the Space as well.

## [Synchronization schedule](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#synchronization-schedule)

- Sync runs automatically every night. The **Next sync** column shows the exact time.
- The initial sync imports all pages and may take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours, depending on the volume of content.
- Subsequent syncs only process updates and are typically much faster.

## [Managing connections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#managing-connections)

Each row has a set of action buttons on the right:

| Button | Action |
| - | - |
| **Test connection** | Verifies that the URL and credentials are still valid. The result is shown as a toast. |
| **Sync now** | Starts an immediate incremental sync. Smartchat follows the run and reports **Sync of … finished.** or **… failed.** Under normal circumstances the nightly sync is sufficient. |
| **Reindex** | Re-imports **all** content from Confluence instead of only the changes. Use it after changing the target collection or when pages are missing. This can take a long time and puts load on the Confluence server, which is why it is disabled after 8:00 PM. |
| **Edit data connection** | Change URL, key, credentials, target collection or the **Active** switch. Leave the credential fields blank to keep the stored ones; enter them again to run the test before saving. The name and type are fixed. |
| **Remove data connection** | Deletes the connection and its schedule. Content already synced into the Space **stays**. |

*\[Image: Reindex confirmation dialog]*

> **Checking ingestion status**
>
> Space Owners can monitor the progress of the sync in the target collection under **Workspace → Knowledge**. Synced pages carry the Confluence icon. Each file shows a **Status**: **Ingested** means the page was processed successfully. Any other status indicates a failure, see [Ingestion Errors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/).

## [How to access the data](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#how-to-access-the-data)

Once the sync has completed, the Confluence content is available in the Smartchat chat interface.

> **Caution**
>
> Synced data is **not** loaded as context automatically. The target collection has to be selected first.

1. Select the Space from the **Space selector** in the top left.
2. Add the target collection (by default **“{Space Name} - General”**) to the chat using the **#** shortcut.

*\[Image: Collections: add the General Space collection with #]*

## [Troubleshooting](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#troubleshooting)

The connection test yields one of the following results:

| Result | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **WORKS** | Connection is healthy. |
| **CONNECTION\_ERROR** | Smartchat cannot reach the server (timeout, DNS failure, connection refused). |
| **MISSING\_CREDENTIALS** | No username or secret was provided. |
| **HTTP\_AUTH\_FAILED** | The credentials were rejected (wrong username/password or expired token). |
| **HTTP\_ERROR\_400** | The request is malformed (usually a wrong URL path or missing parameters). |
| **HTTP\_ERROR\_404** | The URL or space key was not found on the server. |
| **HTTP\_ERROR\_4XX** | Another client-side error (e.g. 403 Forbidden, 429 Rate Limited). |
| **HTTP\_ERROR\_500** | Internal server error on the Confluence side. |
| **HTTP\_ERROR\_5XX** | Another server-side error on the Confluence side. |
| **HTTP\_ERROR** | An unclassified HTTP error. |
| **INVALID\_RESPONSE** | The server answered, but not with the expected Confluence API response, usually a wrong URL path. |
| **FAILED** | An unexpected error occurred. |

### [CONNECTION\_ERROR](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#connection_error)

**Cause:** The Confluence server is unreachable. The URL may be wrong, the server may be down, or there is a network/firewall issue.

**Fix:** Verify the correct Confluence base URL. Data Center instances typically use a path like `https://your-server.example.com/confluence/`. Make sure you are using the API base URL, not the URL you see in the browser when browsing pages.

### [HTTP\_AUTH\_FAILED](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#http_auth_failed)

**Cause:** The username or password is wrong, or the API token has expired or been revoked.

**Fix:** Re-generate the API token in your Confluence account settings and verify that the username matches the token owner.

### [HTTP\_ERROR\_404](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#http_error_404)

**Cause:** Either the base URL path is incorrect (e.g. with or without `/wiki`), or the space key is wrong. The display name may have been used instead of the space key, or there is a typo. Space keys are case-sensitive.

**Fix:** Check the URL path first. Then look up the correct space key in Confluence under **Settings → Space details**.

### [Setup succeeds but ingestion or chat fails](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#setup-succeeds-but-ingestion-or-chat-fails)

**Cause:** The Smartchat Space configuration is incomplete (no API key or default model set). Alternatively, Confluence may be throttling the API with a `429` response due to too many pages being requested at once.

**Fix:** Ensure the Space has a valid [API key and default model](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/) configured before setting up Confluence sync. If you are being rate-limited, check with your Confluence administrator for rate limit settings. You can monitor ingestion status in the target collection.

### [Some or all pages missing after ingestion](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/#some-or-all-pages-missing-after-ingestion)

**Cause:** The API token owner lacks access to the Confluence space, or individual pages have restricted permissions that exclude the token owner.

**Fix:** Ensure the token owner has **read access** to the target Confluence space and all pages within it. Check with your Confluence administrator if page-level restrictions are in place. Then run **Reindex**.

---

# S3 AutoSync

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/

> Automatically sync files from an S3 (OTC OBS) bucket into your Smartchat Space.

S3 AutoSync ingests files from an S3-compatible bucket (OTC Object Storage, OBS) into your Smartchat Space on a schedule. New, changed and removed files in the bucket are picked up and become searchable context for every member of the Space.

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#prerequisites)

- You need the **Space Owner** role in the Smartchat Space. See [Roles](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/roles/) for details.
- An S3 bucket, its endpoint URL and an access key pair with read access to it. Files are uploaded to the bucket with your own tooling (for example `boto3`, the OBS Browser or the Huawei SDK).
- S3 AutoSync must be enabled for your Smartchat environment. If the **S3 AutoSync** page is missing, ask your Application Owner.

> **Uploading with boto3: disable integrity signing**
>
> OTC OBS does not support the S3 request-checksum / integrity signing that recent `boto3` versions (`> 1.36`) enable by default. Uploading with it enabled **corrupts the stored files**: they lose metadata and can no longer be ingested.
>
> When uploading to the bucket with `boto3`, disable it by setting both `request_checksum_calculation` and `response_checksum_validation` to `when_required` on the client config:
>
> ```python
> from botocore.config import Config
>
>
> s3 = boto3.client(
>     "s3",
>     config=Config(
>         request_checksum_calculation="when_required",
>         response_checksum_validation="when_required",
>     ),
> )
> ```
>
> Alternatively, upload via the OBS Browser or the Huawei SDK.

## [Step 1 — Open S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#step-1--open-s3-autosync)

Click your profile image, choose **Administration**, and pick the Space in **Selected Space** under **Space Owner**. Then open **S3 AutoSync**. The table lists the S3 connections of this Space and refreshes itself every minute.

*\[Image: S3 AutoSync page with one active connection]*

## [Step 2 — Add a connection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#step-2--add-a-connection)

Click **Add S3 connection** and fill in the form:

*\[Image: Add S3 connection form with folder rules]*

**Source**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Name** | A name for the connection, shown in the table. |
| **Endpoint URL** | The S3 endpoint, e.g. `https://obs.eu-de.otc.t-systems.com`. |
| **Bucket name** | The bucket to watch: lowercase letters, digits, dots and hyphens. |
| **Region** | The bucket’s region, `eu-de` for OTC. |

**Credentials**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Access key ID** / **Secret access key** | A key pair with read access to the bucket. The values are stored encrypted and never shown again; leave both blank when editing to keep them. |

**Synchronization**

| Field | Description |
| - | - |
| **Sync interval** | How often the bucket is checked: **Every 15 minutes**, **Every hour** (default), **Every 6 hours**, **Every 12 hours**, **Daily** or **Weekly**. |
| **Ingest pipeline** | Only shown when the Space has more than one ingestion configuration. Choose which one processes the synced files. |
| **Target collection** | Where files land that no folder rule covers. **General collection** is the Space’s default collection. Changing it later **moves** already synced files on the next sync. |
| **Folder rules** | Route folders of the bucket into other collections, see [Folder rules](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#folder-rules). |
| **Active** | Leave on. Paused connections keep their settings, but the bucket is not checked. |

The collection does not have to exist yet: **New collection…** in the **Target collection** picker, or in a folder rule’s picker, opens a dialog for its name and an optional description, creates it right away and selects it. The collection stays in the Workspace even if you do not save the connection.

A collection can be created right from the form. It stays even if you do not save the connection.

Click **Save**. Smartchat checks the bucket with the given credentials right away:

- On **create**, an unreachable bucket is rejected. Nothing is stored until endpoint, bucket and keys are correct.
- On **edit**, the connection is saved either way; if the bucket is not reachable the sync is paused (toast **Connection saved, but the bucket is not reachable. The sync stays paused until the settings are fixed.**).

The first run starts with the next interval. Files already in the bucket are ingested on that run; from then on only additions, changes and deletions are processed.

## [Folder rules](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#folder-rules)

By default every file of the bucket lands in the **Target collection** of the connection. If you funnel several data sources into one bucket, you can instead route each folder into its own collection with **folder rules**.

In the form, click **Add folder rule** and enter the folder path inside the bucket (e.g. `reports/2026`) and the **Target collection** for it. Add one row per folder; a folder may appear only once.

### [How folders are matched](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#how-folders-are-matched)

- A rule applies to every object **inside** the folder, at any depth. `reports/2026` matches `reports/2026/q1.pdf` and `reports/2026/archive/old.pdf`.
- Matching stops at folder boundaries: `reports/2026` does **not** match `reports/2026-old/x.pdf`, and a rule `reports` does not match `reportsarchive/x.pdf`.
- If there is a rule for a folder and another rule for one of its subfolders, the rule for the subfolder takes precedence. The order of the rules does not matter.
- Files that no rule covers use the connection’s **Target collection**.
- Leading and trailing slashes are ignored.

Example with the connection’s **Target collection** set to *Misc*:

| Rule | Files | Collection |
| - | - | - |
| `reports/2026` | `reports/2026/q1.pdf` | *Finance 2026* |
| `reports` | `reports/2025/q4.pdf`, `reports/summary.pdf` | *Finance* |
| *(none)* | `reports/2026-old/x.pdf`, `hr/leave.pdf`, `readme.txt` | *Misc* |

### [Changing the rules](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#changing-the-rules)

Changed rules take effect on the **next scheduled sync**. Files that were already synced under the previous rules are **moved**: on the next run AutoSync re-ingests each affected file into its new collection and removes it from the old one, exactly as if the file had changed in the bucket. The same happens when you change the connection’s **Target collection**.

Keep in mind:

- Moving is a re-ingest. A rule that covers many files causes correspondingly many ingestions, processed in batches over consecutive runs.
- A file whose move fails shows up with a failed status in the collection, like any other failed ingestion, and is retried on the next change of that file.
- Only files that AutoSync itself uploaded are moved. A copy of the same file that someone uploaded manually keeps its collection.

## [Monitoring a connection](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#monitoring-a-connection)

| Column | Meaning |
| - | - |
| **Status** | **Active**: scheduled and running. **Paused**: settings kept, bucket not checked. **No schedule**: saved without a schedule yet. |
| **Bucket** | The bucket name; hover for the endpoint URL. |
| **Collection** | The target collection and the number of folder rules. |
| **Schedule** | The interval and **Next:** the time of the next run. |
| **Last sync** | When the last run finished, with counts of **Success**, **Failed** and **Pending** files. |

Click the connection’s **Name** to copy it to the clipboard.

### [Sync statistics](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#sync-statistics)

**Sync statistics** opens a summary of the connection: **All time** totals for **Files processed**, **Added**, **Updated** and **Removed**, and a table of the **Last sync runs** with the same counts per run.

*\[Image: Sync statistics dialog]*

Failed files are listed with their error in the target collection under **Workspace → Knowledge**; see [Ingestion Errors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/) for the meaning of each status.

## [Managing connections](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/#managing-connections)

| Button | Action |
| - | - |
| **Test connection** | Checks whether the bucket is reachable with the stored credentials. |
| **Pause sync** / **Resume sync** | Stops checking the bucket until you resume. Already synced files stay in the Space. |
| **Sync statistics** | Opens the statistics dialog described above. |
| **Edit S3 connection** | Change endpoint, bucket, credentials, interval, target collection or folder rules. |
| **Remove S3 connection** | Deletes the connection and its schedule. Content already synced into the Space **stays**. |

> **No manual run**
>
> Unlike Confluence connections there is no **Sync now** button. Choose a shorter **Sync interval** if you need faster pick-up of new files.

---

# Reviewing Feedback

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/feedback/

> How Space Owners review the ratings members give on responses, and how to switch feedback on or off for a Space.

Members can [rate responses](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/) and, with their consent, share them with you. Space Owners and Application Owners review this feedback in [Administration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/).

The **Feedback** page appears only when feedback is available for your Smartchat environment.

## [Opening the feedback](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/feedback/#opening-the-feedback)

Open **Administration → Space Owner**, pick the Space in **Selected Space** and click **Feedback** under **Manage**.

The list shows the feedback given in this Space with its **Time**, **Sender**, **Model**, rating (**Positive** or **Negative**), **Category** and **Status**. Filter by rating, category, model, status and date, or use **Search comments and chats**. **Open feedback** shows the comment together with the chat up to the rated response.

## [Working through feedback](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/feedback/#working-through-feedback)

- **Mark as read** and **Mark as unread** keep track of what you have looked at.
- **Delete** removes feedback for good. Select several items to mark or delete them together.

Feedback disappears when the member who gave it [withdraws their consent](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/guide/feedback/#withdrawing-your-consent). If your environment deletes feedback after a number of days, the page tells you so.

## [Switching feedback on or off](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/feedback/#switching-feedback-on-or-off)

The **Feedback** switch on the [Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/space-settings/#feedback) settings page decides whether the members of this Space see the rating buttons. Turning it off hides them; feedback given before stays on the **Feedback** page.

# Single Sign-On

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/

> How people sign in to Smartchat through your identity provider, how IdP attributes map to Space and group membership, and the options that let your identity provider decide who has an account and which roles they get.

With single sign-on (SSO), people sign in to Smartchat with their company account. Smartchat sends them to your identity provider, for example Microsoft Entra ID or Active Directory Federation Services (ADFS), which checks their password and any second factor. Their name and email address come from your identity provider and cannot be edited in Smartchat.

T-Systems sets up single sign-on together with the administrators of your identity provider, and configures the options on this page for your instance. Contact T-Systems to switch an option on or off, or to change which values Smartchat reads from your identity provider.

## [Mapping IdP attributes](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#mapping-idp-attributes)

With every sign-in, your identity provider can send IdP attributes of the person, also called claims, for example a role or a group they have in your Active Directory. Smartchat can map an IdP attribute in two ways:

| Mapping | Set up by | Where |
| - | - | - |
| [IdP attribute to Space membership](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-space-membership) | Application Owners | **Application Owner → Spaces**, field **IdP auto-assignment attribute** |
| [IdP attribute to group membership within a Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-group-membership-within-a-space) | Space Owners | **Space Owner → Groups**, field **Identity provider group attributes** |

In both cases, enter the IdP attribute exactly as your identity provider sends it, including spelling, upper and lower case. Ask the administrators of your identity provider for the exact values.

Smartchat reads the IdP attributes every time the person signs in. When your identity provider starts sending an IdP attribute, the person gets what it maps to at their next sign-in. When it stops, they lose it at their next sign-in. What your identity provider assigns cannot be taken away in Administration.

### [IdP attribute to Space membership](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-space-membership)

Each Space can have an **IdP auto-assignment attribute**, set under **Administration → Application Owner → Spaces**, see [Managing Spaces and Users](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/). Everyone whose identity provider sends this IdP attribute becomes a **User** of the Space. Several Spaces can have the same IdP attribute.

Further IdP attributes, agreed with T-Systems during setup, assign roles:

- **Space Owner of a Space**: the Space’s IdP attribute with a Space Owner marker makes the person **Space Owner** of that Space. If no Space has the IdP attribute yet, Smartchat creates the Space, names it after the IdP attribute and sets the IdP attribute. If a Space of that name already exists without the IdP attribute, Smartchat assigns nothing: set the IdP attribute on that Space.
- **Space Owner everywhere**: makes the person **Space Owner** instead of **User** in every Space they get from your identity provider.
- **Application Owner**: makes the person **Application Owner**.

### [IdP attribute to group membership within a Space](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-group-membership-within-a-space)

Space Owners organise the members of their Space in [groups](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/concepts/groups/) under **Administration → Space Owner → Groups**. A group can list **Identity provider group attributes**: everyone whose identity provider sends one of these IdP attributes is added to the group. The group shows them as **Managed by identity provider and cannot be removed manually.**

This only sets group membership. It does not add anyone to the Space: people get into a Space through [IdP attribute to Space membership](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#idp-attribute-to-space-membership), [Space membership by email domain](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#space-membership-by-email-domain) or an administrator.

## [Space membership by email domain](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#space-membership-by-email-domain)

Smartchat can add everyone whose email address belongs to a domain, for example `example.com`, to a Space as **User** when they sign in. This needs no IdP attributes from your identity provider. Removing such a person from the Space only lasts until their next sign-in, when Smartchat adds them again. The settings of that Space cannot be changed in Administration.

## [Optional restrictions](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#optional-restrictions)

T-Systems can enable these options for your instance. Both are off by default.

### [Account creation only through your identity provider](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#account-creation-only-through-your-identity-provider)

With this option enabled, no accounts can be created in Smartchat directly. Instead, a person’s account is created when they first sign in through single sign-on. In Administration:

- People who have never signed in cannot be added to a Space yet. See [People who have never signed in](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/application-owner/#people-who-have-never-signed-in).
- Users cannot be deleted.
- Assigning existing users to Spaces and changing their roles works as usual.

**Users** under **Application Owner** shows: **Users come from the identity provider, so they cannot be created or deleted here. Their spaces and roles can still be changed.**

### [Member and role management only through your identity provider](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#member-and-role-management-only-through-your-identity-provider)

With this option enabled, your identity provider alone decides who belongs to which Space and with which role. It includes everything from [Account creation only through your identity provider](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/single-sign-on/#account-creation-only-through-your-identity-provider), and in addition:

- Neither Application Owners nor Space Owners can add or remove members or change a role in Administration. Administration shows **Users and roles come from the identity provider and cannot be changed here.**
- Every Space needs an **IdP auto-assignment attribute**. A Space cannot be created or saved without one, because the IdP attribute is the only way people get into it.

---

# Uploading Many Files at Once to a Collection via API

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/

> How to add a whole folder of files to a space and put them in a collection, without uploading them one by one.

Uploading files in **Workspace → Collection** works well for a few documents at a time. If you need to add dozens or hundreds — when you are setting up a new space, moving content over from somewhere else, or loading an archive — this guide shows you how to add a whole folder at once and put every file into the collection you choose.

You do this by running a small script from your computer. You do not need to be a developer, but you will be working in a terminal.

> **Is there a better fit?**
>
> If the files change regularly and you want Smartchat to keep up with them automatically, set up a connection instead of doing a one-off load: [S3 AutoSync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/s3-autosync/) watches a storage bucket, and [Confluence Sync](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/confluence-sync/) watches a Confluence space. Use this guide when you have a fixed set of files to add once.

## [Before you start](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#before-you-start)

You will need:

- A Smartchat account that is allowed to add files to the target space
- The **space ID** of the space you are adding to — the script can look this up for you
- The **collection ID** of the collection the files should go into
- The folder of files, on your computer
- Python, set up as described below

## [Set up Python](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#set-up-python)

The script needs **Python 3.10 or newer** and one extra package called `httpx`.

Check which version you have by running this in a terminal:

```bash
python3 --version
```

You will get something like `Python 3.12.5`. The number in the middle is what matters: it must be **10 or higher**.

> **Not sure how to install or upgrade Python?**
>
> We recommend using **uv**, a tool that handles Python versions and packages for you. It downloads the right Python automatically, so you do not have to install or upgrade anything by hand, and it will not interfere with any Python you already have.
>
> Install it by following the [uv installation instructions](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) — one command on macOS, Linux, or Windows.

Every command below is shown two ways. Use the **uv** tab unless you already have a working Python setup you prefer.

## [Get the script](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#get-the-script)

Download it here: [`upload-files-to-collection.py`](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/scripts/upload-files-to-collection.py)

Save it somewhere you can find it, then open a terminal in that folder.

**uv (recommended)**

Nothing else to set up. `uv` reads the requirements from the script itself and takes care of the rest the first time you run it.

**Python only**

Create a throwaway environment next to the script and install `httpx` into it. This keeps the package out of your main Python installation.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
```

Then activate it:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate          # macOS and Linux
.venv\Scripts\activate             # Windows
```

Your prompt now starts with `(.venv)`. Install the package:

```bash
pip install httpx
```

Keep this terminal open — the environment stays active until you close it or run `deactivate`. If you come back later, activate it again before running the script. When you are finished for good, delete the `.venv` folder.

## [Point the script at your Smartchat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#point-the-script-at-your-smartchat)

The script needs the address of your installation’s API gateway. If you do not know it, ask your Smartchat contact. Set it once in the terminal you are working in:

```bash
export SMARTCHAT_GATEWAY=https://<gateway-host>     # macOS and Linux
set SMARTCHAT_GATEWAY=https://<gateway-host>        # Windows
```

You can also pass it to every command as `--gateway https://<gateway-host>`.

## [Step 1 — Find your space ID](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#step-1--find-your-space-id)

**uv (recommended)**

```bash
uv run upload-files-to-collection.py --list-spaces
```

**Python only**

```bash
python upload-files-to-collection.py --list-spaces
```

It asks for your Smartchat email and password, then prints every space you are a member of, with its ID and name. The space you are currently working in is marked with a `*`.

Copy the ID of the space you want to add files to.

> **Note**
>
> If a space you expect is missing, you are not a member of it. Ask a space owner to add you.

## [Step 2 — Find your collection ID](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#step-2--find-your-collection-id)

In Smartchat, open **Workspace → Collection** and open the collection you want to add the files to. Use the **Copy ID** button in the top right of the page.

*\[Image: The Copy ID button in the top right of the collection page]*

That copies the collection ID to your clipboard.

## [Step 3 — Check what will be uploaded](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#step-3--check-what-will-be-uploaded)

Before uploading anything, do a practice run. Add `--dry-run` and the script lists the files it would send, then stops without contacting Smartchat:

**uv (recommended)**

```bash
uv run upload-files-to-collection.py \
  --folder ./my-documents \
  --space-id <your-space-id> \
  --collection-id <your-collection-id> \
  --dry-run
```

**Python only**

```bash
python upload-files-to-collection.py \
  --folder ./my-documents \
  --space-id <your-space-id> \
  --collection-id <your-collection-id> \
  --dry-run
```

Read the list carefully. By default the script picks up **everything** in the folder, including files in subfolders. To narrow it down, add a pattern:

```bash
--glob '**/*.pdf'      # only PDFs, including those in subfolders
--glob '*.pdf'         # only PDFs sitting directly in the folder
--glob '*'             # everything in the folder, but not subfolders
```

Keep the quotes around the pattern.

Hidden files are always left out, whatever pattern you use. That means anything whose name starts with a dot, such as `.DS_Store`, and everything inside hidden folders like `.git`. The script tells you how many it skipped so you can see it happened.

## [Step 4 — Upload](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#step-4--upload)

> **Do not use Smartchat while the script is running**
>
> Leave the Smartchat interface alone from the moment you start the upload until the script prints its summary. **Above all, do not switch to a different space.**
>
> The script works inside whichever space is active for your account. Switching spaces in the browser changes that for your whole account, including the script — files can end up in the wrong space, and there is no automatic way to move them back. Uploading, deleting, or editing files in the UI at the same time can also make the script report failures for files that are actually fine.
>
> If you need to keep using Smartchat, wait for the run to finish, or use a different account for the upload.

When the list looks right, remove `--dry-run` and run it again:

**uv (recommended)**

```bash
uv run upload-files-to-collection.py \
  --folder ./my-documents \
  --space-id <your-space-id> \
  --collection-id <your-collection-id>
```

**Python only**

```bash
python upload-files-to-collection.py \
  --folder ./my-documents \
  --space-id <your-space-id> \
  --collection-id <your-collection-id>
```

The script asks for your password, then works through the files. For each one it shows a spinner with how long it has been waiting, because processing a file takes anything from a few seconds to several minutes depending on its size.

When it finishes it prints a summary: how many files succeeded, how many failed, and why each failure happened. Leave the terminal window open until it is done.

> **Caution**
>
> The first line of every run tells you which Smartchat environment, space, and collection you are about to write to. Check it. There is nothing that asks you to confirm before files start uploading, and files that are already in a space are not automatically replaced.

## [What happens to each file](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#what-happens-to-each-file)

The script does the same three things you would do by hand in the UI, once per file:

1. **Uploads** the file to the space’s storage.
2. **Waits** until the upload has finished storing.
3. **Asks Smartchat to process it** — this is the step that reads the text, splits it into small searchable pieces, and adds it to your collection.

You do not need to do anything afterwards. Putting a file in a collection is part of the processing request, so there is no separate step to add the files to your collection once they are uploaded.

## [Check that it worked](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#check-that-it-worked)

Open the collection in **Workspace → Collection** and refresh the page. Your files should be listed there.

If they are not all showing yet, wait a moment and refresh again — files are added to the collection by a background job, so there is often a short delay between the script finishing and everything appearing.

## [Why a file might be skipped](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#why-a-file-might-be-skipped)

Smartchat avoids storing the same document twice, so some files are deliberately not uploaded. This is the most common reason a run looks like it did nothing:

| What the script reports | What it means | What to do |
| - | - | - |
| `DUPLICATED` | A file with the same name **and** the same contents is already in that folder of the space | Nothing — it is already there |
| `EXISTS` | A file with the same name is already there, but its contents differ | Add `--overwrite` to replace it |
| Nothing appears to happen | The file was uploaded before and already processed | Its contents need to differ from the existing copy |

If you are testing and want a file to go through every time, change **both** its name and its contents.

## [If something goes wrong](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#if-something-goes-wrong)

The script keeps going when one file fails and reports the failures at the end, so a single bad file does not stop the rest.

If a file never shows up, open the collection in **Workspace → Collection**: every file appears there with its current status. [Ingestion Errors](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/ingestion-errors/) explains what each status means and what causes it. Very large files have their own rules, described in [File Size Limits](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/files/file-size-limits/).

Some things worth knowing:

- **Files from subfolders lose their folder.** Only the file name is sent, so `reports/summary.pdf` and `archive/summary.pdf` end up as two files with the same name, and the second is treated as a duplicate or a conflict. Upload such folders one at a time using `--folder-path` to keep them apart.
- **Re-running the script is not free.** Asking Smartchat to process a file again always creates new work, even when the file itself is skipped. Avoid re-running a large batch just to catch a few failures — point the script at a folder holding only the files that failed.
- **Interrupting the script is safe.** Files already uploaded stay uploaded and finish processing on their own. Nothing is left half-written.

## [All options](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#all-options)

| Option | Default | What it does |
| - | - | - |
| `--folder` | — | The folder to upload from (required) |
| `--space-id` | — | The space to upload into (required) |
| `--collection-id` | — | The collection the files go into (required) |
| `--glob` | everything | Which files to pick, as a pattern. Hidden files are always skipped |
| `--dry-run` | — | List the files and stop, without uploading |
| `--list-spaces` | — | Show your spaces and their IDs, then stop |
| `--overwrite` | off | Replace files that already exist with different contents |
| `--folder-path` | — | Put the files in a named folder inside the space |
| `--gateway` | `SMARTCHAT_GATEWAY` | The API gateway address of your Smartchat installation (required unless the environment variable is set) |
| `--scope` | `space` | `space` (shared) or `private` (only you) |
| `--batch-size` | `10` | How many files to send per upload request |
| `--ingestion-config-id` | — | Use one specific processing configuration for all files |
| `-v` | — | Show detailed output, useful when reporting a problem |

You can set your password as the `SMARTCHAT_PASSWORD` environment variable to avoid being asked each run. Anything stored that way is visible to other programs on your machine, so prefer typing it when prompted.

## [For developers](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/user/admin/uploading-many-files/#for-developers)

The script is a worked example of the file-loading API and is meant to be adapted. It uses only the Python standard library plus `httpx`, declared as [inline script metadata](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/inline-script-metadata/) so `uv run` resolves it without a project. Each step is a separate method with the endpoint documented above it.

The calls it makes, in order:

| Step | Call |
| - | - |
| Sign in | `POST /api/v1/auth/user` |
| Set the active space | `GET /user-manager/api/v1/spaces/switch?space_id=` then sign in again |
| Upload | `POST /file-manager/api/v1/files/?file_scope=space` |
| Wait for storage | `GET /file-manager/api/v1/files/{file_id}` until `status` is `uploaded` |
| Look up the processing config | `GET /config-manager/api/v1/space/ingestion/config?file_id=` |
| Request processing | `POST /ingest-master/api/v1/task` with `collectionId` |
| Wait | `GET /ingest-master/api/v1/task/{id}` until `status` is `ingested` |

Three things that are easy to get wrong:

- **Sign in again after switching space.** The active space is carried inside the access token, so a token issued before the switch still points at the old space. The gateway fills in the `x-active-space-id`, `x-user-id` and `x-active-permissions` headers from your token — never set them yourself. This is also why switching spaces in the browser mid-run is dangerous.
- **The first part of the path is a gateway service key, not a repository name.** `file-manager` routes to aifs-files-management. A wrong key returns `404 Service not registered`, which looks like an empty result but is a wrong URL.
- **`collectionId` on the processing request is all you need.** It puts the file in the collection both for search and in the chat interface. `PUT /ingest-master/api/v1/files` exists to repair files that were processed *without* a collection; it is not part of adding new files.

The full API definitions are published per service, and are the authoritative reference:

```plaintext
https://<gateway-host>/file-manager/api/v1/openapi.json
https://<gateway-host>/ingest-master/api/v1/openapi.json
https://<gateway-host>/config-manager/api/v1/openapi.json
https://<gateway-host>/user-manager/api/v1/openapi.json
```

The browsable versions at `/file-manager/redoc` load their content from those same files.

---

# Global KB Guide

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/

> Step-by-step guide to creating a Smartchat session and querying the shared global knowledge base via the RAG API.

# Chat with the Global Knowledge Base

This guide shows how to create a chat session using the shared global knowledge base — no file uploads needed.

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/#prerequisites)

- **Credentials** for a hosted Smartchat RAG API with a `CHAT_USER` role
- A **pre-configured** Smartchat RAG API server

## [1. Authenticate](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/#1-authenticate)

```python
import requests
import json


base_url = "<BASE_URL>"


payload = json.dumps({"username": "<USERNAME>", "password": "<PASSWORD>"})
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}


response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/api/v1/auth/user", headers=headers, data=payload)
headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {response.json()['access_token']}"
```

## [2. Get Default Chat Configuration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/#2-get-default-chat-configuration)

```python
response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/config-manager/api/v1/user/configs", headers=headers)


configs = response.json()
default_config = [c for c in configs if c["userGroupId"] == "default"][0]


default_local_config_id = default_config["localKbConfigs"][0]["id"]
allowed_llms = default_config["localKbConfigs"][0]["allowed_llms"]
```

## [3. Create a Global Chat Session](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/#3-create-a-global-chat-session)

```python
body = {
    "title": "Testing the Smartchat RAG API",
    "config": {
        "localConfigId": default_local_config_id,
        "globalContext": True,
        "chatModel": allowed_llms[0]["name"],
    },
}
response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat-session-manager/api/v1/sessions/", headers=headers, json=body)
session_id = response.json()["sessionId"]
```

## [4. Chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/global-chat/#4-chat)

```python
body = {
    "sessionId": session_id,
    "userPrompt": "Can you summarize the context to me?",
}
response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/query-pipelines/api/v1/chat", headers=headers, json=body)
print(response.json())
```

# Local KB (API only)

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/

> Walk through authentication, session creation, local file upload, ingestion, and prompting with the Smartchat local knowledge base.

# Chat with the Local Knowledge Base

This guide walks through authentication, session creation, local file upload, ingestion, and prompting.

## [Prerequisites](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#prerequisites)

- **Credentials** for a hosted Smartchat RAG API with a `CHAT_USER` role
- A **pre-configured** Smartchat RAG API server
- A **PDF file** to upload

## [1. Authenticate](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#1-authenticate)

```python
import requests
import json


base_url = "<BASE_URL>"


payload = json.dumps({"username": "<USERNAME>", "password": "<PASSWORD>"})
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}


response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/api/v1/auth/user", headers=headers, data=payload)
headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {response.json()['access_token']}"
```

## [2. Get Default Chat Configuration](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#2-get-default-chat-configuration)

```python
response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/config-manager/api/v1/user/configs", headers=headers)


configs = response.json()
default_config = [c for c in configs if c["userGroupId"] == "default"][0]


default_local_config_id = default_config["localKbConfigs"][0]["id"]
allowed_llms = default_config["localKbConfigs"][0]["allowed_llms"]
```

## [3. Upload Files](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#3-upload-files)

```python
import time


file_paths = ["PATH_TO_FILE_1", "PATH_TO_FILE_2"]
params = {"kb": "local"}
files = [("files", open(fp, "rb")) for fp in file_paths]


response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/file-manager/api/v1/files/", headers=headers, params=params, files=files)


pending_files = response.json()
pending_file_ids = [f["fileId"] for f in pending_files]


# Poll until uploaded
while True:
    params = {"kb": "local", "fileIds": pending_file_ids}
    response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/file-manager/api/v1/files/", headers=headers, params=params)
    files = response.json()


    if all(f["status"] in ["uploaded", "duplicated"] for f in files):
        break
    if all(f["status"] in ["error", "file_too_large", "file_type_not_supported"] for f in files):
        raise Exception("Couldn't upload files")
    time.sleep(2)


uploaded_files = files
```

## [4. Ingest Files](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#4-ingest-files)

```python
for uploaded_file in uploaded_files:
    metadata = {
        "file_id": uploaded_file["fileId"],
        "user_id": uploaded_file["userId"],
        "file_name": uploaded_file["fileName"],
        "file_uri": uploaded_file["fileUri"],
    }
    body = {
        "filePath": uploaded_file["fileUri"],
        "role": "user",
        "metadata": metadata,
    }


    requests.post(f"{base_url}/ingest-master/api/v1/task", headers=headers, json=body)


    # Poll until ingested
    while True:
        params = {"file_path": uploaded_file["fileUri"], "role": "user"}
        response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/ingest-master/api/v1/tasks/file", headers=headers, params=params)
        status = response.json()[-1]["status"]


        if status == "ingested":
            break
        if status == "ingestion_failed":
            raise Exception("Couldn't ingest file")


ingested_files = uploaded_files
```

## [5. Create a Chat Session](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#5-create-a-chat-session)

```python
body = {
    "title": "Testing the Smartchat RAG API",
    "config": {
        "localConfigId": default_local_config_id,
        "globalContext": False,
        "activeFiles": [f["fileId"] for f in ingested_files],
        "chatModel": allowed_llms[0]["name"],
    },
}
response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/chat-session-manager/api/v1/sessions/", headers=headers, json=body)
session_id = response.json()["sessionId"]
```

## [6. Chat](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/local-chat/#6-chat)

```python
body = {
    "sessionId": session_id,
    "userPrompt": "Can you summarize the context to me?",
}
response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/query-pipelines/api/v1/chat", headers=headers, json=body)
print(response.json())
```

# RAG API Reference

Source: https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/rag-api/

> HTTP reference for the Smartchat RAG API gateway — covers authentication, service routing, and all available API operations.

Interact with the Smartchat RAG API via HTTP requests. The API is accessed through a gateway with multiple backend services.

## [Base URL & Routing](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/rag-api/#base-url--routing)

Requests follow the format: `<base_url>/<service_path>/<route>`

**Example:** `https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/config-manager/redoc`

| Part | Value |
| - | - |
| Base URL | `https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net` |
| Service path | `config-manager` |
| Route | `redoc` |

## [Authentication](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/rag-api/#authentication)

Obtain a Bearer Token from the [authentication endpoint](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/redoc#tag/Auth/operation/get_user_token_api_v1_auth_user_post), then include the `access_token` in all subsequent requests.

**curl**

```bash
# Authenticate
curl --location '<BASE_URL>/api/v1/auth/user' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "username": "<USERNAME>",
    "password": "<PASSWORD>"
  }'


# Use the token
curl --location '<BASE_URL>/chat-session-manager/api/v1/sessions/' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>'
```

**Python**

```python
import requests
import json


base_url = "<BASE_URL>"


# Authenticate
payload = json.dumps({"username": "<USERNAME>", "password": "<PASSWORD>"})
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
response = requests.post(f"{base_url}/api/v1/auth/user", headers=headers, data=payload)


# Add token to headers
headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {response.json()['access_token']}"


# Make authenticated requests
response = requests.get(f"{base_url}/chat-session-manager/api/v1/sessions/", headers=headers)
print(response.json())
```

## [Services](https://docs.smartchat.ai.t-systems.net/api-reference/rag-api/#services)

| Service | Path | Docs | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
| **API Gateway** | — | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/redoc) | Authentication and entrypoint |
| **Config Manager** | `config-manager` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/config-manager/redoc) | Tenant and RAG configurations |
| **User Manager** | `user-manager` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/user-manager/redoc) | Users, roles, and groups |
| **File Manager** | `file-manager` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/file-manager/redoc) | Files, file groups, knowledge bases |
| **Ingest Master** | `ingest-master` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/ingest-master/redoc) | File ingestion orchestration |
| **Chat Session Manager** | `chat-session-manager` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/chat-session-manager/redoc) | Sessions, history, feedback |
| **Query Pipeline** | `query-pipeline` | [link](https://api-gateway.ai.t-systems.net/query-pipeline/redoc) | Chat response generation |

> **Changed in v3.19.0**
>
> `DELETE /user-manager/api/v1/users/{id}` and `DELETE /user-manager/api/v1/spaces/{id}/full` now also succeed for a user or Space that no longer exists: they answer `204` and `200` instead of `404`.
